header: WeilOddPower — the odd envelope `sin(πx)·P(x)^m` and its transform in closed form; the switched window and its transform. Rung 5, third slice. 2026-09-06.

decls.name: q
decls.why: The odd envelope `sin(πx)·P(x)^m`.

decls.name: q_odd
decls.why: The envelope `q m` is odd: `q m (-x) = -q m x`.

decls.name: continuous_q
decls.why: Helper: the odd envelope `q m` is continuous.

decls.name: sin_pi_mul
decls.why: `sin(πx) = 2·sin(πx/2)·c(x)`.
decls.proves: Real.sin (Real.pi * x) = 2 * Real.sin (Real.pi * x / 2) * c x

decls.name: q_eq
decls.why: The odd envelope is an exact derivative: `q m = −(2/((m+1)π))·f1 (2m+1)`, where `f1 (2m+1)` is the derivative of `c^{2m+2}`.

decls.name: S
decls.why: The odd envelope's transform, `∫₋₁¹ q m x · e^{wx} dx`.

decls.name: ibp_once
decls.why: One integration by parts: `∫ f1 (k+1) · E = −w·∫ c^{k+2} · E`.
decls.proves: (∫ x in (-1 : ℝ)..1, ((f1 (k + 1) x : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.exp (w * (x : ℂ))) = -(w * ∫ x in (-1 : ℝ)..1, ((c x ^ (k + 2) : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.exp (w * (x : ℂ)))

decls.name: S_eq
decls.why: The odd transform through the even one. `S m w = 2w·K (m+1) w/((m+1)π)`.
decls.proves: S m w = 2 * w * K (m + 1) w / (((m : ℂ) + 1) * (Real.pi : ℂ))

decls.name: QS
decls.why: `∏_{j=1}^{m+1}(w² + π²j²)`: the odd transform's denominator.

decls.name: cS
decls.why: `2·π^{2m+1}·(2m+1)!/4^m`: the odd transform's constant.

decls.name: Q_succ_eq
decls.why: The even transform's denominator at `m+1` is `w` times the odd transform's denominator: `Q (m+1) w = w · QS m w`.
decls.proves: Q (m + 1) w = w * QS m w

decls.name: cS_eq
decls.why: The odd transform's constant against the even one's: `cS m · (m+1)π = 2 · cK (m+1)`.

decls.name: S_mul_QS
decls.why: The closed form, multiplied out. `S m w · ∏_{j=1}^{m+1}(w² + π²j²) = 2·π^{2m+1}·(2m+1)!/4^m · sinh w`.
decls.proves: S m w * QS m w = (cS m : ℂ) * Complex.sinh w

decls.name: S_zero_mul
decls.why: At `m = 0`: `S 0 w · (w² + π²) = 2π·sinh w`, the elementary integral of `sin(πx)e^{wx}`.
decls.proves: S 0 w * (w ^ 2 + (Real.pi : ℂ) ^ 2) = 2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.sinh w

decls.name: W
decls.why: The switched window: `sin(πu/h)·P(u/h)^m·cos(γu)`, read on `[−h, h]`.

decls.name: what
decls.why: Its transform, `∫₋ₕʰ W(u)·e^{zu} du`.

decls.name: what_eq
decls.why: The window's transform in closed form. `what h γ m z = (h/2)·[S m ((z + iγ)h) + S m ((z − iγ)h)]`.
decls.proves: what h γ m z = ((h : ℂ) / 2) * (S m ((z + Complex.I * (γ : ℂ)) * (h : ℂ)) + S m ((z - Complex.I * (γ : ℂ)) * (h : ℂ)))

header: WeilOffLine — every term of the zero form is minus a square, and the sign of an off-line zero's own term. Rung 5, first slice of the detection ladder (units 0316–0325). 2026-09-06.

decls.name: SigmaC_neg
decls.why: `Σc` is odd: `sinh` is odd.

decls.name: ghat_neg
decls.why: The window's transform is odd.
decls.proves: ghat h γ (-z) = -ghat h γ z

decls.name: term_eq_neg_sq
decls.why: Every term is minus a square. For any `ρ`, `laplace φ(−ρ)·laplace φ(−(1−ρ)) = −ghat h γ (ρ − 1/2)²`.
decls.proves: laplace (phiC h γ) (-ρ) * laplace (phiC h γ) (-(1 - ρ)) = -(ghat h γ (ρ - 1 / 2)) ^ 2

decls.name: term_re_eq
decls.why: The real part of a term is `(Im g)² − (Re g)²` at `g = ghat h γ (ρ − 1/2)`.
decls.proves: (laplace (phiC h γ) (-ρ) * laplace (phiC h γ) (-(1 - ρ))).re = (ghat h γ (ρ - 1 / 2)).im ^ 2 - (ghat h γ (ρ - 1 / 2)).re ^ 2

decls.name: offPt
decls.why: The off-line point the tuned window reads: `ρ = 1/2 + ε + iγ`.

decls.name: offPt_sub_half
decls.why: Helper: the off-line point minus one half is `offPt ε γ − 1/2 = ε + iγ`.
decls.proves: offPt ε γ - 1 / 2 = (ε : ℂ) + Complex.I * (γ : ℂ)

decls.name: offline_term_le
decls.why: The off-line term is negative. With `g = (h/2)[lobe + Σ(εh)]` and the lobe at most the main term in norm, `term.re ≤ −(h/2)²·Σ(εh)·(Σ(εh) − 2‖lobe‖)`.
needs: hs : ‖SigmaC (((ε : ℂ) + 2 * Complex.I * (γ : ℂ)) * (h : ℂ))‖ ≤ WeilWindow.Sigma (ε * h)
decls.proves: (laplace (phiC h γ) (-offPt ε γ) * laplace (phiC h γ) (-(1 - offPt ε γ))).re ≤ -((h / 2) ^ 2 * (WeilWindow.Sigma (ε * h) * (WeilWindow.Sigma (ε * h) - 2 * ‖SigmaC (((ε : ℂ) + 2 * Complex.I * (γ : ℂ)) * (h : ℂ))‖)))

decls.name: offline_term_le_explicit
decls.why: The same with unit 0319's lobe bound in place of the lobe: for `γ > 0`, if `(2π + π²)·cosh(εh)/(2γh)² ≤ Σ(εh)` then `term.re ≤ −(h/2)²·Σ(εh)·(Σ(εh) − 2(2π + π²)·cosh(εh)/(2γh)²)`.
needs: hs : (2 * Real.pi + Real.pi ^ 2) * Real.cosh (ε * h) / (2 * γ * h) ^ 2 ≤ WeilWindow.Sigma (ε * h)
decls.proves: (laplace (phiC h γ) (-offPt ε γ) * laplace (phiC h γ) (-(1 - offPt ε γ))).re ≤ -((h / 2) ^ 2 * (WeilWindow.Sigma (ε * h) * (WeilWindow.Sigma (ε * h) - 2 * ((2 * Real.pi + Real.pi ^ 2) * Real.cosh (ε * h) / (2 * γ * h) ^ 2))))

header: WeilOnLine — the on-line background, all heights. Rung 4b, second half, slice B3 of the detection ladder (units 0316–0323). 2026-09-06.

decls.name: Psi_neg
decls.why: `Ψ` is odd.

decls.name: term_conj
decls.why: The on-line term is invariant under conjugation of the zero.
decls.proves: (laplace (phiC h γ) (-(starRingEnd ℂ) ρ) * laplace (phiC h γ) (-(1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) ρ))).re = (laplace (phiC h γ) (-ρ) * laplace (phiC h γ) (-(1 - ρ))).re

decls.name: conj_mem
decls.why: Conjugates of nontrivial zeros are nontrivial zeros.

decls.name: conjZ
decls.why: The conjugate, as a nontrivial zero.

decls.name: conjZ_injective
decls.why: Conjugation of nontrivial zeros, `conjZ`, is injective.

decls.name: weightedTerm_conjZ
decls.why: If `0 < h` and the nontrivial zero `ρ` has real part `1/2`, then the weighted term at the conjugate zero equals the weighted term at `ρ`.
decls.proves: weightedTerm h γ (conjZ ρ) = weightedTerm h γ ρ

decls.name: B
decls.why: One side's bound: `A h γ · π²/6`.

decls.name: sum_upper_le
decls.why: Finite on-line sums of height `≥ 11/10`.
decls.proves: ∑ ρ ∈ S, weightedTerm h γ ρ ≤ B h γ

decls.name: sum_lower_le
decls.why: Negative heights. Finite on-line sums of height `≤ −11/10`, by conjugation onto the upper range.
decls.proves: ∑ ρ ∈ S, weightedTerm h γ ρ ≤ B h γ

decls.name: lowSet
decls.why: The on-line zeros of height `|t| ≤ 11/10`, as points.

decls.name: lowU
decls.why: The half-plane `Re z < 3/4`: open, convex, pole-free.

decls.name: lowU_preconnected
decls.why: The half-plane `lowU`, `Re z < 3/4`, is preconnected.

decls.name: lowU_analytic
decls.why: The Riemann zeta function is analytic at every point of the half-plane `lowU`.

decls.name: lowSet_finite
decls.why: The low band is finite.

decls.name: lowCount
decls.why: The low count. Total multiplicity of the on-line zeros of height `|t| ≤ 11/10`. Carried by name.

decls.name: lowCount_nonneg
decls.why: The low count `lowCount` is nonnegative.

decls.name: sum_low_le
decls.why: The low band. Finite on-line sums of height `|t| ≤ 11/10`.
decls.proves: ∑ ρ ∈ S, weightedTerm h γ ρ ≤ 4 * h ^ 2 * lowCount

decls.name: onLineBound
decls.why: The on-line background bound: `2·B h γ + 4h²·lowCount`.

decls.name: sum_onLine_le
decls.why: All heights. Any finite on-line sum is at most `onLineBound`.
decls.proves: ∑ ρ ∈ S, weightedTerm h γ ρ ≤ onLineBound h γ

decls.name: OnLine
decls.why: On-line zeros.

decls.name: sum_onLine_subtype_le
decls.why: If `0 < h` and `11/10 ≤ γ`, then the sum of the weighted terms over any finite set of on-line zeros is at most `onLineBound h γ`.
decls.proves: ∑ ρ ∈ s, weightedTerm h γ ρ.1 ≤ onLineBound h γ

decls.name: tsum_onLine_le
decls.why: The on-line background. For `h > 0` and `γ ≥ 11/10`, the full weighted sum over all on-line zeros is at most `onLineBound h γ`.
decls.proves: ∑' ρ : OnLine, weightedTerm h γ ρ.1 ≤ onLineBound h γ

decls.name: summable_onLine
decls.why: The on-line series is summable.
decls.proves: Summable (fun ρ : OnLine => weightedTerm h γ ρ.1)

decls.name: A_le
decls.why: If `11/10 ≤ γ`, then the crude constant `A h γ` is at most `88·(γ + 3)⁴·(4h² + cFar / h²)`, the band index of `γ` replaced by `γ`.

decls.name: onLineBound_le
decls.why: The on-line background, in `γ` and `h` alone.
decls.proves: onLineBound h γ ≤ 2 * (88 * (γ + 3) ^ 4 * (4 * h ^ 2 + cFar / h ^ 2) * (Real.pi ^ 2 / 6)) + 4 * h ^ 2 * lowCount

header: WeilPower — the m-th power window's transform in closed form. Rung 5, second slice, first module of the switched window (units 0326–0328). 2026-09-06.

decls.name: c
decls.why: The half-angle cosine `c(x) = cos(πx/2)`; `P = c²`.

decls.name: P_eq_c_sq
decls.why: The raised-cosine window is the square of the half-angle cosine: `P x = c x ^ 2`.

decls.name: P_pow
decls.why: The `m`-th power of the window is the `2m`-th power of the half-angle cosine.
decls.proves: P x ^ m = c x ^ (2 * m)

decls.name: c_one
decls.why: The half-angle cosine vanishes at the right endpoint: `c 1 = 0`.

decls.name: c_neg_one
decls.why: The half-angle cosine vanishes at the left endpoint: `c (-1) = 0`.

decls.name: continuous_c
decls.why: Helper: the half-angle cosine `c` is continuous.

decls.name: c_pow_one
decls.why: For `n ≠ 0`, the `n`-th power of the half-angle cosine vanishes at `1`.

decls.name: c_pow_neg_one
decls.why: For `n ≠ 0`, the `n`-th power of the half-angle cosine vanishes at `-1`.

decls.name: hasDerivAt_c
decls.why: The half-angle cosine `c` has derivative `-(π/2)·sin(πx/2)` at every real `x`.

decls.name: hasDerivAt_s
decls.why: The half-angle sine `sin(πy/2)` has derivative `(π/2)·c x` at every real `x`.
decls.proves: HasDerivAt (fun y : ℝ => Real.sin (Real.pi * y / 2)) (Real.pi / 2 * c x) x

decls.name: f1
decls.why: The derivative of `c^{k+1}`.

decls.name: f2
decls.why: The second derivative of `c^{k+2}`.

decls.name: hasDerivAt_f
decls.why: The power `c^{k+1}` of the half-angle cosine has derivative `f1 k x` at every real `x`.
decls.proves: HasDerivAt (fun y : ℝ => c y ^ (k + 1)) (f1 k x) x

decls.name: hasDerivAt_f1
decls.why: The first derivative `f1 (k+1)` of `c^{k+2}` has derivative `f2 k x` at every real `x`.

decls.name: continuous_f1
decls.why: Helper: the first derivative `f1 k` of `c^{k+1}` is continuous.

decls.name: continuous_f2
decls.why: Helper: the second derivative `f2 k` of `c^{k+2}` is continuous.

decls.name: f1_one
decls.why: The derivative `f1 (k+1)` of `c^{k+2}` vanishes at the right endpoint `1`.

decls.name: f1_neg_one
decls.why: The derivative `f1 (k+1)` of `c^{k+2}` vanishes at the left endpoint `-1`.

decls.name: K
decls.why: The envelope's transform, `∫₋₁¹ P(x)^m e^{wx} dx`.

decls.name: hasDerivAt_E
decls.why: For complex `w`, the map `y ↦ e^{wy}` on the reals has derivative `w·e^{wx}` at `x`.
decls.proves: HasDerivAt (fun y : ℝ => Complex.exp (w * (y : ℂ))) (w * Complex.exp (w * (x : ℂ))) x

decls.name: ibp_twice
decls.why: The integral of `c^{k+2} e^{wx}` in terms of the second derivative: `w²·∫ c^{k+2} E = ∫ f2 k · E`.
decls.proves: w ^ 2 * ∫ x in (-1 : ℝ)..1, ((c x ^ (k + 2) : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.exp (w * (x : ℂ)) = ∫ x in (-1 : ℝ)..1, ((f2 k x : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.exp (w * (x : ℂ))

decls.name: K_succ
decls.why: The recurrence. `K (m+1) w · (w² + π²(m+1)²) = (m+1)(2m+1)π²/2 · K m w`.

decls.name: Q
decls.why: `w·∏_{j<m}(w² + π²(j+1)²)`, the denominator of the closed form.

decls.name: cK
decls.why: `2·π^{2m}·(2m)!/4^m`, the numerator's constant.

decls.name: Q_succ
decls.why: The denominator's step: `Q (m+1) w = Q m w · (w² + π²(m+1)²)`.

decls.name: cK_succ
decls.why: The numerator constant's step: `cK (m+1) = (m+1)(2m+1)π²/2 · cK m`.

decls.name: K_zero_mul
decls.why: The base case of the closed form: `K 0 w · w = 2·sinh w` at every complex `w`.

decls.name: K_mul_Q
decls.why: The closed form, multiplied out. `K m w · w·∏_{j=1}^{m}(w² + π²j²) = 2·π^{2m}·(2m)!/4^m · sinh w`.
decls.proves: K m w * Q m w = (cK m : ℂ) * Complex.sinh w

decls.name: cK_one
decls.why: At `m = 1`: `K 1 w · w(w² + π²) = π²·sinh w`, unit 0328's hand check.

decls.name: K_one_mul
decls.why: The closed form at `m = 1`: `K 1 w · w(w² + π²) = π²·sinh w` at every complex `w`.
decls.proves: K 1 w * (w * (w ^ 2 + (Real.pi : ℂ) ^ 2)) = (Real.pi : ℂ) ^ 2 * Complex.sinh w

header: WeilPowerAssembly — block `rung5.md#15` of `lean_stage3/design/rung5.md`, "The conditional theorem: detection under the gap hypothesis". The assembly promised by sections 6, 7, 8, 13g, 13j and 0367; unit 0368, extended by units 0369 (BoxFinite), 0370 (IndicatorContDiff) and the present relay close-out (LOOP.md v21 § 4b).

decls.name: StmtDetectGap
decls.why: The statement. Under the off-line box being nonempty and a detection gap around the max-Re element, some test function of support `L` witnesses the zero form negative.

decls.name: phiW_contDiff_one
decls.why: The switched real window is `C¹`. The unindicated body `W h γ m u · exp(-u/2)` is `C¹` on `ℝ` (product of composable smooth pieces) and its values and derivatives vanish at the endpoints `±h` because `q(m, ±1) = 0` (from `sin(π·±1) = 0`) and `q'(m, ±1) = 0` for `m ≥ 1` (from `P(±1) = cos²(±π/2) = 0`), so `contDiff_one_indicator_Icc` (unit 0370) lifts it to a `C¹` indicator on `[-h, h]`, which is `phiW`.

decls.name: isTest_phiWC
decls.why: The switched window `phiWC` is a `C¹` compactly supported real-valued test function on `[-h, h]`, hence in the class `IsTest (2*h)`. Real-valued by `phiWC_real`; `C¹` via `phiW_contDiff_one` lifted through the real `ofRealCLM`; compact support from `HasCompactSupport.intro` on `Icc (-h) h`; tsupport contained in `Icc (-(2h)/2) ((2h)/2) = Icc (-h) h`.

decls.name: target_lower
decls.why: Target lower. The zero form's term at an off-line zero `ρ` of real part `1/2 + ε` is bounded above by `term_le_at_zero`; the negative of that bound is the target the assembly rides.
needs: hne : QS m (wm h γ (ρ : ℂ)) ≠ 0
hsmall : ‖wm h γ (ρ : ℂ)‖ ^ 2 ≤ Real.pi ^ 2 * ((m : ℝ) + 2) ^ 2 / 2
hq : WeilPowerPhase.q m (wm h γ (ρ : ℂ)) ≤ 1
decls.proves: WeilPowerBands.termW h γ m (ρ : ℂ) ≤ -((h / 2) ^ 2 * ((cS m / D m) ^ 2 * Real.exp (2 * ((wm h γ (ρ : ℂ)) ^ 2).re * sigma m) * (((wm h γ (ρ : ℂ)) ^ 2).re * Real.cos (2 * ((wm h γ (ρ : ℂ)) ^ 2).im * sigma m) - ((wm h γ (ρ : ℂ)) ^ 2).im * Real.sin (2 * ((wm h γ (ρ : ℂ)) ^ 2).im * sigma m)) - (cS m / D m) ^ 2 * ‖wm h γ (ρ : ℂ)‖ ^ 2 * Real.exp (2 * ((wm h γ (ρ : ℂ)) ^ 2).re * sigma m) * (4 * WeilPowerPhase.q m (wm h γ (ρ : ℂ)) + 4 * WeilPowerPhase.q m (wm h γ (ρ : ℂ)) ^ 2) - 2 * (cS m * Real.cosh (((ρ : ℂ).re - 1 / 2) * h) * (2 / (((ρ : ℂ).im + γ) * h) ^ 2) ^ (m + 1)) * ‖S m (wm h γ (ρ : ℂ))‖ - (cS m * Real.cosh (((ρ : ℂ).re - 1 / 2) * h) * (2 / (((ρ : ℂ).im + γ) * h) ^ 2) ^ (m + 1)) ^ 2))

decls.name: near_nonneg
decls.why: Near members. Under the gap hypothesis (`near_set` inside the off-line box carries the block 13g regime per member, expressed as a hypothesis that each near member's term is nonnegative), the weighted sum over the near members is nonnegative. The block 13g regime is folded into `h_pointwise` as an assumption: iterating `WeilPowerNear.term_nonneg` in the current relay pass over the boxed- finite near Finset with each member's F1–F5, R1, R3, R5, L1, N1 witnesses does not close on one try. Sorried with the goal in a comment per LOOP.md § 4b.
needs: h_pointwise : ∀ ρ ∈ near_set, 0 ≤ WeilPowerBands.termW h γ m ρ
decls.proves: 0 ≤ ∑ ρ ∈ near_set, WeilPowerBands.termW h γ m ρ

decls.name: far_moderate_le
decls.why: Far moderate. For zeros with `|ρ.im − γ| ∈ [δ, 1/2]` the count is at most `15 log T + 73` (`JensenCount.zeta_local_zero_count`) and each term has `|termW| ≤ (h/2)² · U_mem²` from `WeilPowerSharp.norm_S_le_c_pos/neg`. The pointwise bound and the count are taken as hypotheses; the assembly is `abs_sum_le_sum_abs` chained with `Finset.sum_le_sum` and `Finset.sum_const`.
needs: h_bound : ∀ ρ ∈ fm_set, |WeilPowerBands.termW h γ m ρ| ≤ (h/2)^2 * U_mem^2
decls.proves: |∑ ρ ∈ fm_set, WeilPowerBands.termW h γ m ρ| ≤ (15 * Real.log T + 73) * ((h/2)^2 * U_mem^2)

decls.name: far_large_le
decls.why: Far large. For zeros with `|ρ.im − γ| > 1/2` the count is at most `15 log T + 698` (unit 0365) and `WeilPowerBounds.norm_S_le_far` gives a super-exponentially small pointwise bound. Same shape as `far_moderate_le`.
needs: h_bound : ∀ ρ ∈ fl_set, |WeilPowerBands.termW h γ m ρ| ≤ (h/2)^2 * U_far^2
decls.proves: |∑ ρ ∈ fl_set, WeilPowerBands.termW h γ m ρ| ≤ (15 * Real.log T + 698) * ((h/2)^2 * U_far^2)

decls.name: on_line_le
decls.why: On-line background. The weighted on-line sum is bounded by `onLineBound h γ m`, from `WeilPowerOnLine.onLineBound_le`.
decls.proves: WeilPowerOnLine.onLineBound h γ m ≤ 2 * (88 * (γ + WeilPowerBands.r h m + 2) ^ 4 * (4 * h ^ 2 + WeilPowerBands.cFarM m / h ^ 2) * (Real.pi ^ 2 / 6)) + 4 * h ^ 2 * WeilOnLine.lowCount

decls.name: detect_gap_exists
decls.why: The assembly. The exponential gap between the target's rate `ε²/(π²(m+2))` and the far-moderate rate `(ε² − δ²)` gives some `L` at which `StmtDetectGap ε T δ L` holds. The proof uses `Real.tendsto_exp_atTop` to close exponential-vs-polynomial, and picks `ρ₀` as a max-Re element of the finite `OffLineBox` (`Stage3.offLineBox_finite`). Sorried on the relay pass — the existence-of-`L` argument depends on `isTest_phiWC` being closed and on the near/far/on-line split being explicit, neither of which stands after one try.
decls.proves: ∃ L : ℝ, StmtDetectGap ε T δ L

header: WeilPowerBackground — the switched window as a test function of the explicit formula, every term of the zero form as minus a square, and the on-line terms bounded. Rung 5, fifth slice. 2026-09-06.

decls.name: phiW
decls.why: The window as a test function of the explicit formula: cut off to `[−h, h]`, times `e^{−u/2}`. Real-valued.

decls.name: phiWC
decls.why: The complex-valued test function WeilDetect reads.

decls.name: phiWC_real
decls.why: The complex-valued test function `phiWC h γ m` has zero imaginary part at every `u`.

decls.name: laplace_phiW
decls.why: The transform in the explicit formula's convention. `laplace φ z = what h γ m (−z − 1/2)`.
decls.proves: laplace (phiWC h γ m) z = what h γ m (-z - 1 / 2)

decls.name: S_eq_sinh
decls.why: The odd envelope's transform through `sinh`: unit 0318's odd-part lemma.
decls.proves: S m w = ∫ x in (-1 : ℝ)..1, ((q m x : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.sinh (w * (x : ℂ))

decls.name: S_neg
decls.why: `S` is odd.

decls.name: what_neg
decls.why: The window's transform is odd.
decls.proves: what h γ m (-z) = -what h γ m z

decls.name: term_eq_neg_sq
decls.why: Every term is minus a square.
decls.proves: laplace (phiWC h γ m) (-ρ) * laplace (phiWC h γ m) (-(1 - ρ)) = -(what h γ m (ρ - 1 / 2)) ^ 2

decls.name: term_re_eq
decls.why: For `h > 0`, the real part of the zero-form term at `ρ` is `(Im ŵ)² − (Re ŵ)²`, where `ŵ` is the window's transform `what h γ m` at `ρ − 1/2`.
decls.proves: (laplace (phiWC h γ m) (-ρ) * laplace (phiWC h γ m) (-(1 - ρ))).re = (what h γ m (ρ - 1 / 2)).im ^ 2 - (what h γ m (ρ - 1 / 2)).re ^ 2

decls.name: PsiW
decls.why: `PsiW m t = ∫₋₁¹ q m x · sin(tx) dx`: the transform on the line, real.

decls.name: S_I_mul
decls.why: `S m (it) = i·PsiW m t`.
decls.proves: S m (Complex.I * (t : ℂ)) = Complex.I * (PsiW m t : ℂ)

decls.name: what_I
decls.why: The window's transform on the line: `what h γ m (it) = i(h/2)[PsiW(h(t+γ)) + PsiW(h(t−γ))]`.
decls.proves: what h γ m (Complex.I * (t : ℂ)) = Complex.I * ((h : ℂ) / 2) * ((PsiW m (h * (t + γ)) : ℂ) + (PsiW m (h * (t - γ)) : ℂ))

decls.name: online_term_eq
decls.why: On the line the term is a real square.
decls.proves: laplace (phiWC h γ m) (-ρ) * laplace (phiWC h γ m) (-(1 - ρ)) = (((h / 2) ^ 2 * (PsiW m (h * (ρ.im + γ)) + PsiW m (h * (ρ.im - γ))) ^ 2 : ℝ) : ℂ)

decls.name: online_term_nonneg
decls.why: For `h > 0` and `ρ` with real part `1/2`, the real part of the zero-form term at `ρ` is nonnegative.
decls.proves: 0 ≤ (laplace (phiWC h γ m) (-ρ) * laplace (phiWC h γ m) (-(1 - ρ))).re

decls.name: PsiW_le_two
decls.why: `|PsiW m t| ≤ 2`.

decls.name: online_term_le_near
decls.why: Near the carrier: the on-line term is at most `4h²`.
decls.proves: (laplace (phiWC h γ m) (-ρ) * laplace (phiWC h γ m) (-(1 - ρ))).re ≤ 4 * h ^ 2

decls.name: PsiW_le_far
decls.why: `|PsiW m t| ≤ cS m·(2/t²)^{m+1}` when `2π²(m+1)² ≤ t²`: unit 0331's far bound at real part zero.

decls.name: online_term_le_far
decls.why: Away from the carrier: for `h|γ_ρ ∓ γ|` both at least `√2·π(m+1)`, the on-line term is at most `(h/2)²·[cS m·(2/(h(γ_ρ−γ))²)^{m+1} + cS m·(2/(h(γ_ρ+γ))²)^{m+1}]²`.
decls.proves: (laplace (phiWC h γ m) (-ρ) * laplace (phiWC h γ m) (-(1 - ρ))).re ≤ (h / 2) ^ 2 * (cS m * (2 / (h * (ρ.im - γ)) ^ 2) ^ (m + 1) + cS m * (2 / (h * (ρ.im + γ)) ^ 2) ^ (m + 1)) ^ 2

header: WeilPowerBands — the on-line background of the switched window over the upper heights: bands, tiles and the explicit band series. Rung 5, seventh slice. 2026-09-06.

decls.name: termW
decls.why: The term of the zero form at the switched window, real part.

decls.name: weightedTermW
decls.why: The term with its multiplicity.

decls.name: termW_nonneg
decls.why: If `0 < h` and `ρ` has real part `1/2`, then the term `termW h γ m ρ` of the zero form at the switched window is nonnegative.

decls.name: weightedTermW_nonneg
decls.why: If `0 < h` and the nontrivial zero `ρ` has real part `1/2`, then the term with its multiplicity, `weightedTermW h γ m ρ`, is nonnegative.

decls.name: band_sum_le
decls.why: Band sum. Unit 0321's, for the switched window.
needs: hM : ∀ ρ ∈ S, termW h γ m ρ ≤ M
decls.proves: ∑ ρ ∈ S, weightedTermW h γ m ρ ≤ M * (15 * Real.log T + 73)

decls.name: sum_by_bands
decls.why: Sum by bands. Unit 0322's.
needs: hM : ∀ ρ ∈ S, termW h γ m ρ ≤ M (idx (ρ : ℂ).im)
decls.proves: ∑ ρ ∈ S, weightedTermW h γ m ρ ≤ ∑ k ∈ S.image (fun ρ : Kadiri.NontrivialZeros => idx (ρ : ℂ).im), M k * (15 * Real.log (centre k) + 73)

decls.name: sum_le_bandSeries
decls.why: For a finite set `S` of zeros on the line with imaginary part at least `11/10`, a nonnegative band bound `M` on the terms and a summable band series, the sum of the weighted terms over `S` is at most the full band series `Σ' k, M k·(15·log(centre k) + 73)`.
needs: hM : ∀ ρ ∈ S, termW h γ m ρ ≤ M (idx (ρ : ℂ).im)
hsum : Summable (fun k : ℕ => M k * (15 * Real.log (centre k) + 73))
decls.proves: ∑ ρ ∈ S, weightedTermW h γ m ρ ≤ ∑' k : ℕ, M k * (15 * Real.log (centre k) + 73)

decls.name: tsum_upper_le
decls.why: Upper on-line sum. Unit 0322's.
needs: hM : ∀ ρ : Kadiri.NontrivialZeros, (ρ : ℂ).re = 1 / 2 → 11 / 10 ≤ (ρ : ℂ).im → termW h γ m ρ ≤ M (idx (ρ : ℂ).im)
hsum : Summable (fun k : ℕ => M k * (15 * Real.log (centre k) + 73))
decls.proves: ∑' ρ : Upper, weightedTermW h γ m ρ.1 ≤ ∑' k : ℕ, M k * (15 * Real.log (centre k) + 73)

decls.name: r
decls.why: The near-band radius, in band steps: `max 1 (5(m+1)/h)`.

decls.name: one_le_r
decls.why: The near-band radius `r h m` is at least `1`.

decls.name: cFarM
decls.why: The far constant: `cS m² · (200/81)² · (10(m+1)²)^{−2m}`.

decls.name: cFarM_nonneg
decls.why: The far constant `cFarM m` is nonnegative.

decls.name: cFarM_le
decls.why: The far constant is polynomial in `m`: `cFarM m ≤ 1000·(m+1)²`.

decls.name: M
decls.why: The dominating band series for the switched window.

decls.name: M_nonneg
decls.why: The dominating band bound `M h γ m k` is nonnegative for every band `k`.

decls.name: term_le_M
decls.why: Domination. Every on-line term of height `≥ 11/10` is at most `M` at its band index.
decls.proves: termW h γ m ρ ≤ M h γ m (idx (ρ : ℂ).im)

decls.name: A
decls.why: The crude constant, with the wider near band.

decls.name: four_h_add_nonneg
decls.why: Helper: the factor `4h² + cFarM m / h²` is nonnegative.

decls.name: A_nonneg
decls.why: The crude constant `A h γ m` is nonnegative.

decls.name: bandTerm_le_A
decls.why: Comparison. Each band term is at most `A/(k+1)³`.
decls.proves: M h γ m k * (15 * Real.log (centre k) + 73) ≤ A h γ m / ((k : ℝ) + 1) ^ 3

decls.name: bandSeries_summable
decls.why: Summability of the band series.
decls.proves: Summable (fun k : ℕ => M h γ m k * (15 * Real.log (centre k) + 73))

decls.name: bandSeries_le
decls.why: The band series in closed form: at most `A·π²/6`.
decls.proves: ∑' k : ℕ, M h γ m k * (15 * Real.log (centre k) + 73) ≤ A h γ m * (Real.pi ^ 2 / 6)

decls.name: tsum_upper_le_explicit
decls.why: Upper on-line background.
decls.proves: ∑' ρ : Upper, weightedTermW h γ m ρ.1 ≤ A h γ m * (Real.pi ^ 2 / 6)

decls.name: A_le
decls.why: If `11/10 ≤ γ`, then the crude constant `A h γ m` is at most `88·(γ + r h m + 2)⁴·(4h² + cFarM m / h²)`, the band index of `γ` replaced by `γ`.
decls.proves: A h γ m ≤ 88 * (γ + r h m + 2) ^ 4 * (4 * h ^ 2 + cFarM m / h ^ 2)

decls.name: tsum_upper_le_explicit'
decls.why: Upper on-line background, in `γ`, `h` and `m` alone: `≤ 88·(γ + r + 2)⁴·(4h² + cFarM m/h²)·π²/6`.
decls.proves: ∑' ρ : Upper, weightedTermW h γ m ρ.1 ≤ 88 * (γ + r h m + 2) ^ 4 * (4 * h ^ 2 + cFarM m / h ^ 2) * (Real.pi ^ 2 / 6)

header: WeilPowerBounds — bounds on the odd transform read off its polynomial. Rung 5, fourth slice. 2026-09-06.

decls.name: factor_eq
decls.why: One factor of the product, factored: `w² + a² = (w − ia)(w + ia)`.
decls.proves: w ^ 2 + (a : ℂ) ^ 2 = (w - Complex.I * (a : ℂ)) * (w + Complex.I * (a : ℂ))

decls.name: norm_factor_ge
decls.why: Each factor has norm at least `(Re w)²`.

decls.name: QS_factor
decls.why: The product `QS m w` written as `∏_{j<m+1} (w² + (π(j+1))²)`, each `π(j+1)` a real cast.
decls.proves: QS m w = ∏ j ∈ Finset.range (m + 1), (w ^ 2 + ((Real.pi * ((j : ℝ) + 1) : ℝ) : ℂ) ^ 2)

decls.name: QS_ne_zero
decls.why: If `Re w ≠ 0`, then the product `QS m w` is nonzero.

decls.name: cS_pos
decls.why: The constant `cS m` of the closed form is positive.

decls.name: S_eq_div'
decls.why: Wherever the product is nonzero the closed form is a quotient.
decls.proves: S m w = (cS m : ℂ) * Complex.sinh w / QS m w

decls.name: S_eq_div
decls.why: If `Re w ≠ 0`, then the odd transform is the quotient `S m w = cS m · sinh w / QS m w`.
decls.proves: S m w = (cS m : ℂ) * Complex.sinh w / QS m w

decls.name: norm_S_le'
decls.why: The norm of the quotient, bounded by `cosh(Re w)` over the product's norm.
decls.proves: ‖S m w‖ ≤ cS m * Real.cosh w.re / ‖QS m w‖

decls.name: norm_S_le
decls.why: Upper bound. `‖S m w‖ ≤ cS m · cosh(Re w) / ‖QS m w‖` for `Re w ≠ 0`.
decls.proves: ‖S m w‖ ≤ cS m * Real.cosh w.re / ‖QS m w‖

decls.name: norm_factor_ge_far
decls.why: Far up in height each factor is at least half the height squared.

decls.name: norm_QS_ge_far
decls.why: `‖QS m w‖ ≥ ((Im w)²/2)^{m+1}` when `2·((Re w)² + π²(m+1)²) ≤ (Im w)²`.

decls.name: norm_S_le_far
decls.why: Far bound. `‖S m w‖ ≤ cS m · cosh(Re w) · (2/(Im w)²)^{m+1}` when `2·((Re w)² + π²(m+1)²) ≤ (Im w)²`.
decls.proves: ‖S m w‖ ≤ cS m * Real.cosh w.re * (2 / w.im ^ 2) ^ (m + 1)

decls.name: Ps
decls.why: The real product `∏_{j=1}^{m+1}(s² + π²j²)`.

decls.name: Ps_pos
decls.why: The real product `Ps m s` is positive for every real `s`.

decls.name: QS_ofReal
decls.why: At a real point `s` the product `QS m s` is the cast of the real product `Ps m s`.
decls.proves: QS m (s : ℂ) = ((Ps m s : ℝ) : ℂ)

decls.name: S_real_eq
decls.why: At real `s` the transform is real: `cS m · sinh s / ∏(s² + π²j²)`.
decls.proves: S m (s : ℂ) = ((cS m * Real.sinh s / Ps m s : ℝ) : ℂ)

decls.name: Ps_le
decls.why: `Ps m s ≤ (s² + π²(m+1)²)^{m+1}`.

decls.name: sinh_ge
decls.why: `sinh s ≥ e^s/4` for `s ≥ 1`.

decls.name: S_real_ge
decls.why: Lower bound at the target. For `1 ≤ s`, `cS m · e^s / (4·(s² + π²(m+1)²)^{m+1}) ≤ Re (S m s)`.
decls.proves: cS m * Real.exp s / (4 * (s ^ 2 + Real.pi ^ 2 * ((m : ℝ) + 1) ^ 2) ^ (m + 1)) ≤ (S m (s : ℂ)).re

header: WeilPowerBridge — the term at an actual zero: two sidebands, the far one bounded. Rung 5, twentieth slice; worksheet § 13 block 13j. 2026-09-07.

decls.name: wp
decls.why: The far sideband: `w₊ = (ρ − 1/2 + iγ)h`.

decls.name: wm
decls.why: The near sideband: `w₋ = (ρ − 1/2 − iγ)h`.

decls.name: im_sq_sub_re_sq
decls.why: `Im(z)² − Re(z)² = −Re(z²)`: the arithmetic that turns the background's term into a square.

decls.name: term_eq_sidebands
decls.why: The term of the zero form at `ρ`, read at the two sidebands: the window is a cosine at height `γ` times an envelope, so `what` is `(h/2)(S₊ + S₋)` and the term is `−(h/2)²` times the real part of its square.
decls.proves: WeilPowerBands.termW h γ m ρ = -((h / 2) ^ 2 * (((S m (wm h γ ρ)) ^ 2).re + 2 * (S m (wp h γ ρ) * S m (wm h γ ρ)).re + ((S m (wp h γ ρ)) ^ 2).re))

decls.name: term_le_sidebands
decls.why: The same term with the two unbounded pieces sent to their norms: `Re(S₊S₋) ≥ −‖S₊‖‖S₋‖` and `Re(S₊²) ≥ −‖S₊‖²`, and a larger bracket makes the term more negative.
decls.proves: WeilPowerBands.termW h γ m ρ ≤ -((h / 2) ^ 2 * (((S m (wm h γ ρ)) ^ 2).re - 2 * ‖S m (wp h γ ρ)‖ * ‖S m (wm h γ ρ)‖ - ‖S m (wp h γ ρ)‖ ^ 2))

decls.name: wp_im
decls.why: `Im w₊ = (ρ.im + γ)h`: the far sideband sits at about `2γh` when `ρ` is near height `γ`.

decls.name: far_sideband_le
decls.why: The far sideband is § 4's decay: once the far condition holds at `w₊`, `‖S m w₊‖` is `cS m·cosh((ρ.re − 1/2)h)` times `(2/((ρ.im + γ)h)²)^(m+1)`.
decls.proves: ‖S m (wp h γ ρ)‖ ≤ cS m * Real.cosh ((ρ.re - 1 / 2) * h) * (2 / ((ρ.im + γ) * h) ^ 2) ^ (m + 1)

decls.name: term_le_at_zero
decls.why: The term at an actual nontrivial zero of zeta, every constant explicit: 13b's lower bound on the near sideband, § 4's decay on the far one, and the cross term between them. This is the ladder attached to a zero.
needs: hne : QS m (wm h γ (ρ : ℂ)) ≠ 0
hsmall : ‖wm h γ (ρ : ℂ)‖ ^ 2 ≤ Real.pi ^ 2 * ((m : ℝ) + 2) ^ 2 / 2
hq : q m (wm h γ (ρ : ℂ)) ≤ 1
decls.proves: WeilPowerBands.termW h γ m (ρ : ℂ) ≤ -((h / 2) ^ 2 * ((cS m / D m) ^ 2 * Real.exp (2 * ((wm h γ (ρ : ℂ)) ^ 2).re * sigma m) * (((wm h γ (ρ : ℂ)) ^ 2).re * Real.cos (2 * ((wm h γ (ρ : ℂ)) ^ 2).im * sigma m) - ((wm h γ (ρ : ℂ)) ^ 2).im * Real.sin (2 * ((wm h γ (ρ : ℂ)) ^ 2).im * sigma m)) - (cS m / D m) ^ 2 * ‖wm h γ (ρ : ℂ)‖ ^ 2 * Real.exp (2 * ((wm h γ (ρ : ℂ)) ^ 2).re * sigma m) * (4 * q m (wm h γ (ρ : ℂ)) + 4 * q m (wm h γ (ρ : ℂ)) ^ 2) - 2 * (cS m * Real.cosh (((ρ : ℂ).re - 1 / 2) * h) * (2 / (((ρ : ℂ).im + γ) * h) ^ 2) ^ (m + 1)) * ‖S m (wm h γ (ρ : ℂ))‖ - (cS m * Real.cosh (((ρ : ℂ).re - 1 / 2) * h) * (2 / (((ρ : ℂ).im + γ) * h) ^ 2) ^ (m + 1)) ^ 2))

header: WeilPowerClean — the clean shell. Rung 5, eighteenth slice; worksheet § 13 block 13h. 2026-09-07.

decls.name: blocked_card_le
decls.why: One member's blocked shells sit inside `W + 1` consecutive shells: the shell scale `a * ρ ^ k` climbs by the factor `ρ`, while the window `[lo, hi]` does not move.
needs: hB : ∀ k ∈ B, lo ≤ d * (a * ρ ^ k) ∧ d * (a * ρ ^ k) ≤ hi

decls.name: exists_unblocked
decls.why: More shells than the members can block leaves one shell in no member's blocking set.
decls.proves: ∃ k, k < K ∧ ∀ j ∈ S, k ∉ B j

decls.name: exists_clean_shell
decls.why: The clean shell: `blocked_card_le` at each member, then `exists_unblocked` at `W + 1`.
needs: hB : ∀ j ∈ S, ∀ k ∈ B j, lo ≤ d j * (a * ρ ^ k) ∧ d j * (a * ρ ^ k) ≤ hi
decls.proves: ∃ k, k < K ∧ ∀ j ∈ S, k ∉ B j

decls.name: exists_clean_shell_of_count
decls.why: The same with the member count given by a bound `N`.
needs: hB : ∀ j ∈ S, ∀ k ∈ B j, lo ≤ d j * (a * ρ ^ k) ∧ d j * (a * ρ ^ k) ≤ hi
decls.proves: ∃ k, k < K ∧ ∀ j ∈ S, k ∉ B j

header: WeilPowerCompare — the comparison at another off-line zero. Rung 5, ninth slice, worksheet section 7. 2026-09-06.

decls.name: cP
decls.why: The strong Gaussian coefficient `1/(π²(m+1))`: the exponent's rate where `Re(w²) ≥ 0`.

decls.name: cE
decls.why: The weak Gaussian coefficient `(m+2)/(π²(2m+3)²)`: the rate where `Re(w²) ≤ 0`, and the one the target's lower bound carries.

decls.name: cQ
decls.why: The quartic error coefficient `1/(π⁴(m+1)³)`.

decls.name: cP_pos
decls.why: The strong Gaussian coefficient `cP m` is positive.

decls.name: cE_pos
decls.why: The weak Gaussian coefficient `cE m` is positive.

decls.name: cQ_pos
decls.why: The quartic error coefficient `cQ m` is positive.

decls.name: cE_le_cP
decls.why: `(m+1)(m+2) ≤ (2m+3)²`, so the weak coefficient is at most the strong one.

decls.name: Eup
decls.why: The upper exponent, both signs of `Re(w²)` in one expression: `max _ 0` picks the strong coefficient where `Re(w²) ≥ 0` and the weak one elsewhere.

decls.name: Elow
decls.why: The lower exponent at the target, on the real axis.

decls.name: norm_S_le_gauss
decls.why: The Gaussian upper bound, both signs in one exponent.
decls.proves: ‖S m w‖ ≤ 4 / (Real.pi * ((m : ℝ) + 1)) * ‖w‖ * Real.exp (Eup m w)

decls.name: S_real_ge_low
decls.why: The Gaussian lower bound at the target, in the `Elow` form.
decls.proves: 4 / (Real.pi * ((m : ℝ) + 1) * (2 * (m : ℝ) + 3)) * s * Real.exp (Elow m s) ≤ (S m (s : ℂ)).re

decls.name: S_real_pos
decls.why: The target's transform is positive on the real axis inside the regime.

decls.name: compare_le
decls.why: The comparison at another off-line zero. The transform at any point of the regime is at most `2m+3` times `‖w‖/s` times the exponential of the exponent difference, times the target's transform.
decls.proves: ‖S m w‖ ≤ (2 * (m : ℝ) + 3) * (‖w‖ / s) * Real.exp (Eup m w - Elow m s) * (S m (s : ℂ)).re

decls.name: wOf
decls.why: The point the window reads at a zero of real-part offset `ε` and height offset `Δ`: `w = (ε + iΔ)h`.

decls.name: wOf_re
decls.why: The real part of the point `wOf ε Δ h = (ε + iΔ)h` is `ε·h`.

decls.name: wOf_im
decls.why: The imaginary part of the point `wOf ε Δ h = (ε + iΔ)h` is `Δ·h`.

decls.name: wOf_sq_re
decls.why: The real part of the square of `wOf ε Δ h` is `(ε² − Δ²)·h²`.

decls.name: norm_wOf_sq
decls.why: The squared norm of `wOf ε Δ h` is `(ε² + Δ²)·h²`.

decls.name: norm_wOf_pow4
decls.why: The fourth power of the norm of `wOf ε Δ h` is `((ε² + Δ²)·h²)²`.

decls.name: QS_ne_zero_wOf
decls.why: If `ε ≠ 0` and `h ≠ 0`, then `QS m` is nonzero at the point `wOf ε Δ h`.

decls.name: rate
decls.why: The quadratic rate of the exponent difference, per unit `h²`.

decls.name: qerr
decls.why: The quartic error of the exponent difference, per unit `h⁴`.

decls.name: exponent_eq
decls.why: The exponent difference in the worksheet's variables, with no sign hypothesis: a quadratic rate against a quartic error.
decls.proves: Eup m (wOf ε' Δ h) - Elow m (ε * h) = rate m ε' Δ ε * h ^ 2 + qerr m ε' Δ ε * h ^ 4

decls.name: rate_eq_of_le
decls.why: At `Δ² ≥ ε'²` the rate is `−cE·(Δ² + ε² − ε'²)`.
decls.proves: rate m ε' Δ ε = -(cE m * (Δ ^ 2 + ε ^ 2 - ε' ^ 2))

decls.name: rate_neg_of_le
decls.why: A zero above the target in height is suppressed at every real part. `Δ² ≥ ε'²` and `0 < ε` make the rate negative with no condition on `ε'`.

decls.name: rate_neg_of_ge
decls.why: A zero inside the target's height is suppressed when its real part does not exceed the target's by the constant `cE/cP`.
needs: hlt : cP m * (ε' ^ 2 - Δ ^ 2) < cE m * ε ^ 2

decls.name: qerr_pos
decls.why: The quartic error is positive at any target with `0 < ε`.

decls.name: rate_neg_of_qerr
decls.why: The range condition on `h` already forces the rate negative.
needs: hq : qerr m ε' Δ ε * h ^ 2 ≤ -rate m ε' Δ ε / 2

decls.name: compare_suppressed
decls.why: Suppression at another off-line zero. For `h` in the range where the quartic error is at most half the rate — which by `rate_neg_of_qerr` already makes the rate negative — the transform at the other zero is an exponentially small multiple of the target's.
needs: hq : qerr m ε' Δ ε * h ^ 2 ≤ -rate m ε' Δ ε / 2
decls.proves: ‖S m (wOf ε' Δ h)‖ ≤ (2 * (m : ℝ) + 3) * (‖wOf ε' Δ h‖ / (ε * h)) * Real.exp (rate m ε' Δ ε * h ^ 2 / 2) * (S m ((ε * h : ℝ) : ℂ)).re

header: WeilPowerCount — the short-interval count leaf, and the range that closes. Rung 5, nineteenth slice; worksheet § 13 block 13i. 2026-09-07.

decls.name: StmtShortCount
decls.why: The short-interval zero-count leaf: the number of zeros the target carries at height `T` is at most `c₁ log T + c₂`. Budget `c₁ ≤ 0.48`; route: Backlund plus `ArgCrude.StmtSCrude`, see the module header.

decls.name: card_le_of_leaf
decls.why: A member set counted by the leaf is bounded by `c₁ log T + c₂`.

decls.name: exists_range_log
decls.why: The closure: with `α = c₁(W+1)lρ < 1` there is an `L ≥ 0` — namely `(c₂(W+1)lρ + E + αD)/(1 − α)` — at which the shells fit for every count parameter `M` below `D + L`. This is what removes unit 0351's circularity: the demand is linear in `L` and the coefficient is `α`.
decls.proves: ∃ L : ℝ, 0 ≤ L ∧ ∀ M : ℝ, 0 ≤ M → M ≤ D + L → (c₁ * M + c₂) * ((W : ℝ) + 1) * lρ + E ≤ L

decls.name: count_lt_shells
decls.why: The shell count in `ℕ`, read off the same inequality scaled by `lρ`.

decls.name: exists_clean_shell_of_leaf
decls.why: 13h's clean shell with the member count supplied by the leaf rather than assumed.
needs: hN : c₁ * Real.log T + c₂ ≤ (N : ℝ)
hB : ∀ j ∈ S, ∀ k ∈ B j, lo ≤ d j * (a * ρ ^ k) ∧ d j * (a * ρ ^ k) ≤ hi
decls.proves: ∃ k, k < K ∧ ∀ j ∈ S, k ∉ B j

header: WeilPowerGauss — the odd transform in the Gaussian regime, through Euler's product for `sinh`. Rung 5, sixth slice. 2026-09-06.

decls.name: g
decls.why: One factor of Euler's product for `sinh`: `1 + w²/(π²(j+1)²)`.

decls.name: euler_sinh
decls.why: Euler's product for `sinh`. `w·∏_{j<n}(1 + w²/(π²(j+1)²)) → sinh w`.
decls.proves: Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => w * ∏ j ∈ Finset.range n, g w j) atTop (𝓝 (Complex.sinh w))

decls.name: D_pos
decls.why: The product `D m` is positive.

decls.name: D_eq
decls.why: The product `D m` in closed form: `D m = π^(2(m+1))·((m+1)!)²`.

decls.name: QS_eq_D_mul
decls.why: The head of the closed form's product is `D m` times the head of Euler's product.
decls.proves: QS m w = (D m : ℂ) * ∏ j ∈ Finset.range (m + 1), g w j

decls.name: cprime_eq
decls.why: `cS m / D m = centralBinom (m+1) / (π (m+1) 4^m)`.
decls.proves: cS m / D m = ((Nat.centralBinom (m + 1) : ℕ) : ℝ) / (Real.pi * ((m : ℝ) + 1) * 4 ^ m)

decls.name: cprime_le
decls.why: The constant `cS m / D m` is at most `4/(π(m+1))`.

decls.name: cprime_ge
decls.why: The constant `cS m / D m` is at least `4/(π(m+1)(2m+3))`.

decls.name: cprime_pos
decls.why: The constant `cS m / D m` is positive.

decls.name: T
decls.why: The tail of Euler's product from `m+1` to `n`.

decls.name: tendsto_S
decls.why: The transform as a limit of tails.
decls.proves: Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => ((cS m / D m : ℝ) : ℂ) * w * T m w n) atTop (𝓝 (S m w))

decls.name: exp_le_one_add
decls.why: `exp(x − x²) ≤ 1 + x` for real `0 ≤ x ≤ 1/2`.

decls.name: norm_x_le
decls.why: Each tail factor's argument is within `1/2` of `0` when `‖w‖² ≤ π²(m+2)²/2`.

decls.name: x_re
decls.why: Helper: the real part of a factor's argument `w²/(π²(j+1)²)` is `Re(w²)/(π²(j+1)²)`.

decls.name: x_norm
decls.why: Helper: the norm of a factor's argument `w²/(π²(j+1)²)` is `‖w‖²/(π²(j+1)²)`.

decls.name: norm_T_le
decls.why: The tail's norm is at most the exponential of the tail sums.
decls.proves: ‖T m w n‖ ≤ Real.exp ((w ^ 2).re / Real.pi ^ 2 * ∑ j ∈ Finset.Ico (m + 1) n, 1 / ((j : ℝ) + 1) ^ 2 + ‖w‖ ^ 4 / Real.pi ^ 4 * ∑ j ∈ Finset.Ico (m + 1) n, 1 / ((j : ℝ) + 1) ^ 4)

decls.name: norm_T_le_pos
decls.why: If `‖w‖² ≤ π²(m+2)²/2` and `0 ≤ Re(w²)`, then the tail product `T m w n` has norm at most `exp(Re(w²)/(π²(m+1)) + ‖w‖⁴/(π⁴(m+1)³))` for every `n`.
decls.proves: ‖T m w n‖ ≤ Real.exp ((w ^ 2).re / (Real.pi ^ 2 * ((m : ℝ) + 1)) + ‖w‖ ^ 4 / (Real.pi ^ 4 * ((m : ℝ) + 1) ^ 3))

decls.name: norm_T_le_neg
decls.why: If `‖w‖² ≤ π²(m+2)²/2`, `Re(w²) ≤ 0` and `2m+3 ≤ n`, then the tail product `T m w n` has norm at most `exp(Re(w²)·(m+2)/(π²(2m+3)²) + ‖w‖⁴/(π⁴(m+1)³))`.

decls.name: norm_S_le_gauss_pos
decls.why: Upper bound, Gaussian regime, `Re(w²) ≥ 0`.

decls.name: norm_S_le_gauss_neg
decls.why: Upper bound, Gaussian regime, `Re(w²) ≤ 0`.

decls.name: Tr
decls.why: The tail at real `s` is a real product.

decls.name: T_ofReal
decls.why: At a real point `s` the tail product `T m s n` is the cast of the real tail `Tr m s n`.
decls.proves: T m (s : ℂ) n = ((Tr m s n : ℝ) : ℂ)

decls.name: Tr_ge
decls.why: The real tail is at least the exponential of the tail sums.

decls.name: S_real_ge_gauss
decls.why: Lower bound at the target, Gaussian regime. For `0 < s`, `4/(π(m+1)(2m+3)) · s · exp(s²(m+2)/(π²(2m+3)²) − s⁴/(π⁴(m+1)³)) ≤ Re (S m s)`.

header: WeilPowerGeom — the geometric sum and the harmonic correction: the two sums the averaging route needs over a range of `h`, one bounded independently of the range length, the other by a logarithm of it. Rung 5, fourteenth slice; worksheet § 13 block 13d. 2026-09-06.

decls.name: Mab
decls.why: The larger endpoint value of the geometric factor: `exp(z.re(m+½)/π²)` is monotone in `m`, so on `[a, b]` it is at most this.

decls.name: geomBound
decls.why: The geometric sum's bound: the two endpoint values over the separation of `ρ = exp(z/π²)` from `1`, which Jordan's inequality makes `2 z.im/π³` times `exp(z.re/π²)`. It does not grow with `b − a`.

decls.name: norm_one_sub_exp_ge
decls.why: The separation of `exp w` from `1`, from the imaginary part alone.

decls.name: sin_im_ge
decls.why: Jordan's inequality at the phase `z.im/π²`, linear in `z.im`.

decls.name: rho_ne_one
decls.why: The ratio `ρ = exp(z/π²)` is not `1`: its distance to `1` is at least `exp(z.re/π²)·2 z.im/π³ > 0`.

decls.name: exp_shift
decls.why: The geometric factorization of the shifted exponential.
decls.proves: Complex.exp (z * ((m : ℂ) + 1 / 2) / (Real.pi : ℂ) ^ 2) = Complex.exp (z / (2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) ^ 2)) * Complex.exp (z / (Real.pi : ℂ) ^ 2) ^ m

decls.name: geom_Ico
decls.why: The geometric series over `Ico a b`; Mathlib's `geom_sum_Ico`, which this Mathlib does state (as a `lemma`, so a `theorem`-only grep misses it).
decls.proves: ∑ m ∈ Finset.Ico a b, x ^ m = (x ^ b - x ^ a) / (x - 1)

decls.name: norm_geom_le
decls.why: The geometric sum is bounded independently of the range length.
decls.proves: ‖∑ m ∈ Finset.Ico a b, Complex.exp (z * ((m : ℂ) + 1 / 2) / (Real.pi : ℂ) ^ 2)‖ ≤ geomBound z a b

decls.name: exp_lin_le_Mab
decls.why: The geometric factor at an interior `m` is at most its value at an endpoint: the exponent is linear in `m`, so the sign of `z.re` picks the end.
decls.proves: Real.exp (z.re * ((m : ℝ) + 1 / 2) / Real.pi ^ 2) ≤ Mab z a b

decls.name: log_step
decls.why: One harmonic step against the logarithm, `1/(m+1) ≤ log(m+1) − log m`.

decls.name: log_telescope
decls.why: The harmonic sum over `Ico a b` is at most `log b − log a`.
decls.proves: ∀ b : ℕ, a ≤ b → ∑ m ∈ Finset.Ico a b, 1 / ((m : ℝ) + 1) ≤ Real.log b - Real.log a

decls.name: harmonic_quarter
decls.why: The correction sum's majorant, `(log b − log a)/(4π²)`.
decls.proves: ∑ m ∈ Finset.Ico a b, 1 / (Real.pi ^ 2 * (4 * (m : ℝ) + 6)) ≤ (Real.log b - Real.log a) / (4 * Real.pi ^ 2)

decls.name: norm_corr_le
decls.why: One term's correction, `2‖z‖·r m` times the geometric factor.
decls.proves: ‖Complex.exp (z * (u m : ℂ)) - Complex.exp (z * ((m : ℂ) + 1 / 2) / (Real.pi : ℂ) ^ 2)‖ ≤ Real.exp (z.re * ((m : ℝ) + 1 / 2) / Real.pi ^ 2) * (2 * ‖z‖) * (u m - ((m : ℝ) + 1 / 2) / Real.pi ^ 2)

decls.name: norm_sum_exp_u_le
decls.why: The averaged sum: bounded by the range-free geometric bound plus a logarithm of the range.
decls.proves: ‖∑ m ∈ Finset.Ico a b, Complex.exp (z * (u m : ℂ))‖ ≤ geomBound z a b + 2 * ‖z‖ * Mab z a b * ((Real.log b - Real.log a) / (4 * Real.pi ^ 2))

header: WeilPowerGeomGen — the geometric bound with a free slope, and `u` at general `λ`. Rung 5, fifteenth slice; worksheet § 13 block 13e. 2026-09-06.

decls.name: MabGen
decls.why: The larger endpoint value of the geometric factor at a free slope.

decls.name: geomBoundGen
decls.why: The geometric sum's bound at a free slope: the two endpoint values over the separation of `ρ = exp(zα)` from `1`, which Jordan's inequality makes `2 z.im α/π` times `exp(z.re α)`. It does not grow with `b − a`, and it grows like `1/α` as the slope falls.

decls.name: uLam
decls.why: The normalized tail sum at general `λ`: `uLam λ h = h²·σ(λh − 1)`, which is `u(λh − 1)/λ²` whenever `1 ≤ λh`.

decls.name: exp_shift_gen
decls.why: The geometric factorization of the affine exponential.
decls.proves: Complex.exp (z * ((α * (h : ℝ) + β₀ : ℝ) : ℂ)) = Complex.exp (z * ((β₀ : ℝ) : ℂ)) * Complex.exp (z * ((α : ℝ) : ℂ)) ^ h

decls.name: sin_im_ge_gen
decls.why: Jordan's inequality at the phase `z.im·α`, linear in `z.im·α`.

decls.name: rho_ne_one_gen
decls.why: The ratio `ρ = exp(zα)` is not `1`: its distance to `1` is at least `exp(z.re α)·2 z.im α/π > 0`.

decls.name: norm_geom_le_gen
decls.why: The geometric sum at a free slope is bounded independently of the range length.
decls.proves: ‖∑ h ∈ Finset.Ico a b, Complex.exp (z * ((α * (h : ℝ) + β₀ : ℝ) : ℂ))‖ ≤ geomBoundGen z α β₀ a b

decls.name: exp_lin_le_MabGen
decls.why: The geometric factor at an interior `h` is at most its value at an endpoint: the exponent is affine and increasing in `h`, so the sign of `z.re` picks the end.
decls.proves: Real.exp (z.re * (α * (h : ℝ) + β₀)) ≤ MabGen z α β₀ a b

decls.name: norm_corr_le_gen
decls.why: One term's correction at a free scale, `2‖z‖·c/(h+1)` times the geometric factor.
decls.proves: ‖Complex.exp (z * (u h : ℂ)) - Complex.exp (z * ((α * (h : ℝ) + β₀ : ℝ) : ℂ))‖ ≤ Real.exp (z.re * (α * (h : ℝ) + β₀)) * (2 * ‖z‖) * (c / ((h : ℝ) + 1))

decls.name: norm_sum_exp_u_le_gen
decls.why: The averaged sum at a free slope: bounded by the range-free geometric bound plus a logarithm of the range.
decls.proves: ‖∑ h ∈ Finset.Ico a b, Complex.exp (z * (u h : ℂ))‖ ≤ geomBoundGen z α β₀ a b + 2 * ‖z‖ * c * MabGen z α β₀ a b * (Real.log b - Real.log a)

decls.name: uLam_eq
decls.why: `uLam` is `u` rescaled: `uLam λ h = u(λh − 1)/λ²`, the cast `((λh − 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1 = λh` being the whole content.
decls.proves: uLam lam h = WeilPowerSigma.u (lam * h - 1) / (lam : ℝ) ^ 2

decls.name: uLam_bracket
decls.why: The bracket for `uLam` at general `λ`: slope `1/(λπ²)`, intercept `−1/(2λ²π²)`, correction scale `1/(2λ³π²)`.
decls.proves: 0 ≤ uLam lam h - ((h : ℝ) / ((lam : ℝ) * Real.pi ^ 2) - 1 / (2 * (lam : ℝ) ^ 2 * Real.pi ^ 2)) ∧ uLam lam h - ((h : ℝ) / ((lam : ℝ) * Real.pi ^ 2) - 1 / (2 * (lam : ℝ) ^ 2 * Real.pi ^ 2)) ≤ 1 / (2 * (lam : ℝ) ^ 3 * Real.pi ^ 2) / ((h : ℝ) + 1)

header: WeilPowerNear — the near members' sign. Rung 5, seventeenth slice; worksheet § 13 block 13g. 2026-09-07.

decls.name: uLam_nonneg
decls.why: The window's phase argument is nonnegative at every `h`.

decls.name: uLam_le
decls.why: The upper half of `uLam_bracket`, with the intercept absorbed: the correction `1/(2λ³π²(h+1))` is under `1/(2λ²π²)` exactly when `λ(h+1) ≥ 1`.
decls.proves: WeilPowerGeomGen.uLam lam h ≤ (h : ℝ) / ((lam : ℝ) * Real.pi ^ 2)

decls.name: cos_ge_lin
decls.why: `cos` above its chord on `[0, π/2]`: `Real.mul_le_sin` at `π/2 − θ`.

decls.name: bracket_nonneg
decls.why: The bracket's sign under the crude condition N2.
decls.proves: 0 ≤ (e' ^ 2 - D ^ 2) * Real.cos θ - 2 * e' * D * Real.sin θ

decls.name: re_term_eq
decls.why: The weighted term's real part, explicit.
decls.proves: (WeilPowerShell.coef e' D e * Complex.exp (WeilPowerShell.zOf e' D e * (u : ℂ))).re = Real.exp (2 * (e' ^ 2 - D ^ 2 - e ^ 2) * u) / e ^ 2 * ((e' ^ 2 - D ^ 2) * Real.cos (4 * e' * D * u) - 2 * e' * D * Real.sin (4 * e' * D * u))

decls.name: phase_le
decls.why: The phase is largest at the top of the range.
decls.proves: 4 * e' * D * WeilPowerGeomGen.uLam lam h ≤ 4 * e' * D * ((b : ℝ) / ((lam : ℝ) * Real.pi ^ 2))

decls.name: term_nonneg
decls.why: One near member's term is nonnegative at every `h` in the range.
decls.proves: 0 ≤ (WeilPowerShell.coef e' D e * Complex.exp (WeilPowerShell.zOf e' D e * ((WeilPowerGeomGen.uLam lam h : ℝ) : ℂ))).re

decls.name: shellSum_nonneg
decls.why: The near member's shell sum is nonnegative: it helps the target.
decls.proves: 0 ≤ WeilPowerShell.shellSum e' D e lam a b

decls.name: shellSum_nonneg_abs
decls.why: The same with `|Δ|`, the sign of `Δ` split off through `shellSum_neg`.
decls.proves: 0 ≤ WeilPowerShell.shellSum e' D e lam a b

header: WeilPowerOnLine — the switched window's on-line background, all heights. Rung 5, eighth slice. 2026-09-06.

decls.name: PsiW_neg
decls.why: `PsiW` is odd.

decls.name: term_conj
decls.why: The on-line term is invariant under conjugation of the zero.
decls.proves: termW h γ m ((starRingEnd ℂ) ρ) = termW h γ m ρ

decls.name: weightedTermW_conjZ
decls.why: For `h > 0` and a nontrivial zero `ρ` with real part `1/2`, the weighted on-line term at the conjugate zero `conjZ ρ` equals the weighted on-line term at `ρ`.
decls.proves: weightedTermW h γ m (conjZ ρ) = weightedTermW h γ m ρ

decls.name: B
decls.why: One side's bound: `A h γ m · π²/6`.

decls.name: sum_upper_le
decls.why: Finite on-line sums of height `≥ 11/10`.
decls.proves: ∑ ρ ∈ S, weightedTermW h γ m ρ ≤ B h γ m

decls.name: sum_lower_le
decls.why: Negative heights.
decls.proves: ∑ ρ ∈ S, weightedTermW h γ m ρ ≤ B h γ m

decls.name: sum_low_le
decls.why: The low band. Finite on-line sums of height `|t| ≤ 11/10`.
decls.proves: ∑ ρ ∈ S, weightedTermW h γ m ρ ≤ 4 * h ^ 2 * lowCount

decls.name: onLineBound
decls.why: The on-line background bound: `2·B h γ m + 4h²·lowCount`.

decls.name: sum_onLine_le
decls.why: All heights.
decls.proves: ∑ ρ ∈ S, weightedTermW h γ m ρ ≤ onLineBound h γ m

decls.name: sum_onLine_subtype_le
decls.why: For `h > 0` and `γ ≥ 11/10`, the sum of the weighted on-line terms over any finite set of on-line zeros is at most `onLineBound h γ m`.
decls.proves: ∑ ρ ∈ s, weightedTermW h γ m ρ.1 ≤ onLineBound h γ m

decls.name: tsum_onLine_le
decls.why: The on-line background of the switched window.
decls.proves: ∑' ρ : OnLine, weightedTermW h γ m ρ.1 ≤ onLineBound h γ m

decls.name: summable_onLine
decls.why: The on-line series is summable.
decls.proves: Summable (fun ρ : OnLine => weightedTermW h γ m ρ.1)

decls.name: onLineBound_le
decls.why: The on-line background, in `γ`, `h` and `m` alone.
decls.proves: onLineBound h γ m ≤ 2 * (88 * (γ + r h m + 2) ^ 4 * (4 * h ^ 2 + cFarM m / h ^ 2) * (Real.pi ^ 2 / 6)) + 4 * h ^ 2 * lowCount

header: WeilPowerPhase — the phase of the tail product: `S m w` is its principal part `c·w·exp(w²σ)` up to a relative error `2q`, and `Re (S m w)²` has an explicit lower bound. Rung 5, twelfth slice; worksheet § 13 requirement (b). 2026-09-06. Unit 0347.

decls.name: hterm
decls.why: The summand of the tail sum, `1/(π²(j+1)²)`.

decls.name: sigmaN
decls.why: The partial tail sum `σ_n`.

decls.name: sigma
decls.why: The full tail sum `σ = Σ_{j ≥ m+1} 1/(π²(j+1)²)`.

decls.name: summable_hterm
decls.why: The tail-sum summands `1/(π²(j+1)²)` are summable over `j`.

decls.name: summable_shift
decls.why: The summands shifted by `m + 1`, `k ↦ hterm (k + (m + 1))`, are summable.

decls.name: sigmaN_eq
decls.why: The partial tail sum `σ_n` equals `1/π²` times the sum of `1/(j+1)²` over `m+1 ≤ j < n`.
decls.proves: sigmaN m n = 1 / Real.pi ^ 2 * ∑ j ∈ Finset.Ico (m + 1) n, 1 / ((j : ℝ) + 1) ^ 2

decls.name: sigmaN_tendsto
decls.why: The partial tail sums `σ_n` converge to the full tail sum `σ` as `n → ∞`.
decls.proves: Tendsto (fun n => sigmaN m n) atTop (𝓝 (sigma m))

decls.name: sigma_le
decls.why: Upper bound on the full tail sum: `σ ≤ 1/(π²(m+1))`.

decls.name: sigma_ge
decls.why: Lower bound on the full tail sum: `1/(π²(m+2)) ≤ σ`.

decls.name: x
decls.why: `x_j = w²/(π²(j+1)²)`, so that `g w j = 1 + x w j`.

decls.name: g_eq
decls.why: The product factor `g w j` is `1 + x w j`, by definition.
decls.proves: g w j = 1 + x w j

decls.name: x_eq_mul
decls.why: `x w j` is `w²` times the tail-sum summand `hterm j`, cast to `ℂ`.
decls.proves: x w j = w ^ 2 * ((hterm j : ℝ) : ℂ)

decls.name: g_ne_zero
decls.why: If `‖w‖² ≤ π²(m+2)²/2` and `m + 1 ≤ j`, then the product factor `g w j` is nonzero.

decls.name: T_eq_exp
decls.why: If `‖w‖² ≤ π²(m+2)²/2`, the tail product `T m w n` is the exponential of the sum of `log (g w j)` over `m+1 ≤ j < n`.
decls.proves: T m w n = Complex.exp (∑ j ∈ Finset.Ico (m + 1) n, Complex.log (g w j))

decls.name: delta
decls.why: `δ_n = Σ (log(1 + x_j) − x_j)`.

decls.name: norm_log_sub_le
decls.why: If `‖w‖² ≤ π²(m+2)²/2` and `m + 1 ≤ j`, then `‖log (g w j) − x w j‖ ≤ ‖x w j‖²`.
decls.proves: ‖Complex.log (g w j) - x w j‖ ≤ ‖x w j‖ ^ 2

decls.name: q
decls.why: The quartic error `q = ‖w‖⁴/(π⁴(m+1)³)`.

decls.name: q_nonneg
decls.why: The quartic error `q m w` is nonnegative.

decls.name: norm_delta_le
decls.why: If `‖w‖² ≤ π²(m+2)²/2`, the exponent remainder satisfies `‖δ_n‖ ≤ q` for every `n`.
decls.proves: ‖delta m w n‖ ≤ q m w

decls.name: T_eq_mul
decls.why: The split. `T m w n = exp(w² σ_n) · exp(δ_n)`.
decls.proves: T m w n = Complex.exp (w ^ 2 * ((sigmaN m n : ℝ) : ℂ)) * Complex.exp (delta m w n)

decls.name: norm_exp_delta_sub_one_le
decls.why: If `‖w‖² ≤ π²(m+2)²/2` and `q ≤ 1`, then `‖exp(δ_n) − 1‖ ≤ 2q` for every `n`.
decls.proves: ‖Complex.exp (delta m w n) - 1‖ ≤ 2 * q m w

decls.name: P
decls.why: The principal part `P = exp(w² σ)`.

decls.name: P_tendsto
decls.why: The exponentials `exp(w² σ_n)` converge to the principal part `P = exp(w² σ)` as `n → ∞`.
decls.proves: Tendsto (fun n => Complex.exp (w ^ 2 * ((sigmaN m n : ℝ) : ℂ))) atTop (𝓝 (P m w))

decls.name: norm_S_sub_le
decls.why: The principal part carries `S` up to `2q`.
decls.proves: ‖S m w - ((cS m / D m : ℝ) : ℂ) * w * P m w‖ ≤ 2 * q m w * ‖((cS m / D m : ℝ) : ℂ) * w * P m w‖

decls.name: norm_A_sq
decls.why: The squared norm of the principal term `c·w·P`, `c = cS m / D m`, equals `c² ‖w‖² exp(2 Re(w²) σ)`.
decls.proves: ‖((cS m / D m : ℝ) : ℂ) * w * P m w‖ ^ 2 = (cS m / D m) ^ 2 * ‖w‖ ^ 2 * Real.exp (2 * (w ^ 2).re * sigma m)

decls.name: re_A_sq
decls.why: The real part of the principal part squared, explicitly.
decls.proves: ((((cS m / D m : ℝ) : ℂ) * w * P m w) ^ 2).re = (cS m / D m) ^ 2 * Real.exp (2 * (w ^ 2).re * sigma m) * ((w ^ 2).re * Real.cos (2 * (w ^ 2).im * sigma m) - (w ^ 2).im * Real.sin (2 * (w ^ 2).im * sigma m))

decls.name: re_sq_ge
decls.why: The lower bound on `Re (S m w)²`.
decls.proves: ((((cS m / D m : ℝ) : ℂ) * w * P m w) ^ 2).re - ‖((cS m / D m : ℝ) : ℂ) * w * P m w‖ ^ 2 * (4 * q m w + 4 * q m w ^ 2) ≤ ((S m w) ^ 2).re

decls.name: re_S_sq_ge
decls.why: The deliverable.
decls.proves: (cS m / D m) ^ 2 * Real.exp (2 * (w ^ 2).re * sigma m) * ((w ^ 2).re * Real.cos (2 * (w ^ 2).im * sigma m) - (w ^ 2).im * Real.sin (2 * (w ^ 2).im * sigma m)) - (cS m / D m) ^ 2 * ‖w‖ ^ 2 * Real.exp (2 * (w ^ 2).re * sigma m) * (4 * q m w + 4 * q m w ^ 2) ≤ ((S m w) ^ 2).re

header: WeilPowerSelect — selection of the target. Rung 5, tenth slice, worksheet section 8. 2026-09-06.

decls.name: farDelta_le
decls.why: Far heights need no selection. A zero with real part offset in `[0, 1/2]` and height offset at least `1/2` already has `ε'² ≤ Δ²`, with no choice of target at all.

decls.name: exists_step_le
decls.why: The pigeonhole lemma. A sequence, nonnegative at `0` and bounded above by `B` at every step, cannot climb by more than `δ` at every one of `N` steps once `N·δ > B`. Monotonicity of `f` is not needed: boundedness at each step is already enough to stop the climb.
decls.proves: ∃ k < N, f (k + 1) ≤ f k + δ

decls.name: δSel
decls.why: The step size, `K'π²λ/h`.

decls.name: δSel_pos
decls.why: If `K'`, `lam` and `h` are positive, then the step size `δSel K' lam h` is positive.

decls.name: exists_target_step
decls.why: The step exists, with its height explicit. `E`'s square cannot climb by more than `δSel K' λ h` at every step past `h/(4K'π²λ)`.
needs: hbound : ∀ k, 0 ≤ E k ∧ E k ≤ 1 / 2
decls.proves: ∃ k : ℕ, (k : ℝ) ≤ h / (4 * K' * Real.pi ^ 2 * lam) ∧ (E (k + 1)) ^ 2 ≤ (E k) ^ 2 + δSel K' lam h

decls.name: target_bound
decls.why: Selection of the target. There is a step `k`, at height at most `h/(4K'π²λ)` above the box's own step, whose `(k+1)`-neighbours all meet the cluster's criterion against `E k`.
needs: hbound : ∀ k, 0 ≤ E k ∧ E k ≤ 1 / 2
decls.proves: ∃ k : ℕ, (k : ℝ) ≤ h / (4 * K' * Real.pi ^ 2 * lam) ∧ ∀ ε', 0 ≤ ε' → ε' ≤ E (k + 1) → ε' ^ 2 ≤ (E k) ^ 2 + δSel K' lam h

decls.name: target_height_le
decls.why: The step's height above the box: `T + k/2 ≤ T + h/(8K'π²λ)`.
needs: hk : (k : ℝ) ≤ h / (4 * K' * Real.pi ^ 2 * lam)
decls.proves: T + (k : ℝ) / 2 ≤ T + h / (8 * K' * Real.pi ^ 2 * lam)

decls.name: target_ge_box
decls.why: The target's own real-part offset is at least the box zero's.

header: WeilPowerSharp — the Gaussian bounds with the constant kept exact and the tail sum sharp: the two lost factors of WeilPowerGauss removed. Rung 5, eleventh slice. 2026-09-06. Unit 0346; the decision is unit 0345.

decls.name: sum_telescope
decls.why: Telescoping sum over the tail.

decls.name: sum_inv_sq_ge_sharp
decls.why: The sharp lower bound for the tail sum: `1/(m+2) − 1/(n+1)`.

decls.name: Tr_ge_sharp
decls.why: Tail product lower bound with the sharp sum.

decls.name: S_real_ge_sharp
decls.why: Lower bound at the target, sharp. The constant is `cS m / D m` itself and the rate is `s²/(π²(m+2))`.
decls.proves: cS m / D m * s * Real.exp (s ^ 2 / (Real.pi ^ 2 * ((m : ℝ) + 2)) - s ^ 4 / (Real.pi ^ 4 * ((m : ℝ) + 1) ^ 3)) ≤ (S m (s : ℂ)).re

decls.name: norm_S_le_c_pos
decls.why: Upper bound, `Re(w²) ≥ 0`, constant kept.
decls.proves: ‖S m w‖ ≤ cS m / D m * ‖w‖ * Real.exp ((w ^ 2).re / (Real.pi ^ 2 * ((m : ℝ) + 1)) + ‖w‖ ^ 4 / (Real.pi ^ 4 * ((m : ℝ) + 1) ^ 3))

decls.name: norm_S_le_c_neg
decls.why: Upper bound, `Re(w²) ≤ 0`, constant kept. The exponent is unit 0333's.

decls.name: compare_sharp
decls.why: The comparison with no lost factor. For `0 ≤ Re(w²)`, `0 < s`, both in the regime, `‖S m w‖ ≤ (‖w‖/s) · exp(E) · Re (S m s)` with `E = (Re(w²) − s²)/(π²(m+1)) + s²/(π²(m+1)(m+2)) + (‖w‖⁴ + s⁴)/(π⁴(m+1)³)`.

header: WeilPowerShell — one shell member's weighted sum, explicit. Rung 5, sixteenth slice; worksheet § 13 block 13f. 2026-09-06.

decls.name: zOf
decls.why: The exponent's coefficient at the shell member `ζ = ε' + iΔ` against the target at `ε`: `z = 2(ζ² − ε²)`.

decls.name: coef
decls.why: The member's weight relative to the target: `ζ²/ε²`.

decls.name: uSh
decls.why: `uLam` patched at `0` to the affine value, so that the bracket G7 of block 13e holds at every `k` and not only at `k ≥ 1`.

decls.name: shellSum
decls.why: One shell member's weighted sum over the range `[a, b)`.

decls.name: zOf_re
decls.why: The real part of the exponent's coefficient.

decls.name: zOf_im
decls.why: The imaginary part of the exponent's coefficient: the phase's rate.

decls.name: norm_zOf_le
decls.why: The size of the exponent's coefficient.

decls.name: norm_coef
decls.why: The member's weight, in size.

decls.name: uSh_bracket
decls.why: The bracket G7 for the patched sequence, at every `k` including `0`.
decls.proves: ∀ k : ℕ, 0 ≤ uSh lam k - ((k : ℝ) / ((lam : ℝ) * Real.pi ^ 2) - 1 / (2 * (lam : ℝ) ^ 2 * Real.pi ^ 2)) ∧ uSh lam k - ((k : ℝ) / ((lam : ℝ) * Real.pi ^ 2) - 1 / (2 * (lam : ℝ) ^ 2 * Real.pi ^ 2)) ≤ 1 / (2 * (lam : ℝ) ^ 3 * Real.pi ^ 2) / ((k : ℝ) + 1)

decls.name: sum_uSh_eq
decls.why: The patch does not change the sum: over `Ico a b` with `1 ≤ a` no index is `0`.
decls.proves: ∑ h ∈ Finset.Ico a b, coef e' D e * Complex.exp (zOf e' D e * ((WeilPowerGeomGen.uLam lam h : ℝ) : ℂ)) = ∑ h ∈ Finset.Ico a b, coef e' D e * Complex.exp (zOf e' D e * ((uSh lam h : ℝ) : ℂ))

decls.name: im_alpha_le
decls.why: Jordan's hypothesis G3 holds at the shell's phase: `4ε'Δ ≤ 1` and `1/(λπ²) ≤ 1/9 < π/2`.
decls.proves: (zOf e' D e).im * (1 / ((lam : ℝ) * Real.pi ^ 2)) ≤ Real.pi / 2

decls.name: norm_zOf_c_le
decls.why: The hypothesis G6 holds: `‖z‖ ≤ 3/2` and `c ≤ 1/18`, so the product is under `1 ≤ a + 1`.
decls.proves: ‖zOf e' D e‖ * (1 / (2 * (lam : ℝ) ^ 3 * Real.pi ^ 2)) ≤ (a : ℝ) + 1

decls.name: exp_end_le
decls.why: The geometric factor at an interior index is at most `M = e^{2ηb/(λπ²)}`: the exponent is nonnegative and at most `αb`, and `z.re ≤ 2η`.
decls.proves: Real.exp ((zOf e' D e).re * (1 / ((lam : ℝ) * Real.pi ^ 2) * (k : ℝ) + -1 / (2 * (lam : ℝ) ^ 2 * Real.pi ^ 2))) ≤ Real.exp (2 * eta * (b : ℝ) / ((lam : ℝ) * Real.pi ^ 2))

decls.name: MabGen_le
decls.why: The endpoint factor is at most `M`.
decls.proves: WeilPowerGeomGen.MabGen (zOf e' D e) (1 / ((lam : ℝ) * Real.pi ^ 2)) (-1 / (2 * (lam : ℝ) ^ 2 * Real.pi ^ 2)) a b ≤ Real.exp (2 * eta * (b : ℝ) / ((lam : ℝ) * Real.pi ^ 2))

decls.name: inv_exp_le
decls.why: The reciprocal of the ratio's modulus, bounded by the size of `z`.
decls.proves: 1 / Real.exp ((zOf e' D e).re * (1 / ((lam : ℝ) * Real.pi ^ 2))) ≤ Real.exp (2 * (e' ^ 2 + D ^ 2 + e ^ 2) * (1 / ((lam : ℝ) * Real.pi ^ 2)))

decls.name: geomBound_le
decls.why: The geometric part of the shell member's bound, explicit in `ε', Δ, ε, η, λ, b`.
decls.proves: WeilPowerGeomGen.geomBoundGen (zOf e' D e) (1 / ((lam : ℝ) * Real.pi ^ 2)) (-1 / (2 * (lam : ℝ) ^ 2 * Real.pi ^ 2)) a b ≤ Real.exp (2 * eta * (b : ℝ) / ((lam : ℝ) * Real.pi ^ 2)) * (lam : ℝ) * Real.pi ^ 3 * Real.exp (2 * (e' ^ 2 + D ^ 2 + e ^ 2) * (1 / ((lam : ℝ) * Real.pi ^ 2))) / (4 * e' * D)

decls.name: shellSum_le
decls.why: One shell member's weighted sum, explicit. The geometric part does not grow with the range; the correction grows like its logarithm.
decls.proves: |shellSum e' D e lam a b| ≤ (e' ^ 2 + D ^ 2) / e ^ 2 * Real.exp (2 * eta * (b : ℝ) / ((lam : ℝ) * Real.pi ^ 2)) * ((lam : ℝ) * Real.pi ^ 3 * Real.exp (2 * (e' ^ 2 + D ^ 2 + e ^ 2) * (1 / ((lam : ℝ) * Real.pi ^ 2))) / (4 * e' * D) + 2 * (e' ^ 2 + D ^ 2 + e ^ 2) * (Real.log b - Real.log a) / ((lam : ℝ) ^ 3 * Real.pi ^ 2))

decls.name: shellSum_neg
decls.why: The sum is even in `Δ`: the member at `ε' − iΔ` is the conjugate of the member at `ε' + iΔ`, and the real part does not see the conjugation.
decls.proves: shellSum e' (-D) e lam a b = shellSum e' D e lam a b

decls.name: shellSum_le_abs
decls.why: The bound at a signed `Δ`, through the evenness.
decls.proves: |shellSum e' D e lam a b| ≤ (e' ^ 2 + |D| ^ 2) / e ^ 2 * Real.exp (2 * eta * (b : ℝ) / ((lam : ℝ) * Real.pi ^ 2)) * ((lam : ℝ) * Real.pi ^ 3 * Real.exp (2 * (e' ^ 2 + |D| ^ 2 + e ^ 2) * (1 / ((lam : ℝ) * Real.pi ^ 2))) / (4 * e' * |D|) + 2 * (e' ^ 2 + |D| ^ 2 + e ^ 2) * (Real.log b - Real.log a) / ((lam : ℝ) ^ 3 * Real.pi ^ 2))

decls.name: sum_telescope_amgm

header: WeilPowerTail — the tail bound: an upper bound on `‖S m w‖` for every `w`, with no regime. Block 16a of `lean_stage3/design/rung5.md` (section 16, its line T12). 2026-11-22. Priced in unit 0378.

decls.name: sum_inv_pow4_le_third

decls.name: norm_one_add_le
decls.why: `‖1 + z‖ ≤ exp(Re z + ‖z‖²/2)`, for every complex `z`.

decls.name: norm_g_le
decls.why: One factor of the tail product.
decls.proves: ‖g w j‖ ≤ Real.exp ((w ^ 2).re * hterm j + ‖w‖ ^ 4 * hterm j ^ 2 / 2)

decls.name: norm_T_le_tail

decls.proves: ‖T m w n‖ ≤ Real.exp ((w ^ 2).re * sigmaN m n + ‖w‖ ^ 4 / (6 * Real.pi ^ 4 * ((m : ℝ) + 1) ^ 3))

decls.name: norm_S_le_tail

decls.proves: ‖S m w‖ ≤ cS m / D m * ‖w‖ * Real.exp ((w ^ 2).re * sigma m + ‖w‖ ^ 4 / (6 * Real.pi ^ 4 * ((m : ℝ) + 1) ^ 3))

header: WeilSeries — the band series made explicit. Rung 4b, second half, slice B2 of the detection ladder (units 0316–0322). 2026-09-06.

decls.name: cFar

decls.name: M

decls.name: M_nonneg

decls.name: dist_ge

decls.proves: (laplace (phiC h γ) (-(ρ : ℂ)) * laplace (phiC h γ) (-(1 - (ρ : ℂ)))).re ≤ M h γ (idx (ρ : ℂ).im)

decls.name: A_nonneg

decls.name: weight_le

decls.name: bandSeries_le

header: WeilTiles — the heights tiled by bands. Rung 4b, second half, slice B1 of the detection ladder (units 0316–0321). 2026-09-06.

decls.name: centre

decls.name: idx_spec

header: WeilTransform — the transform of the tuned window in closed form. Rung 3 of the detection ladder (units 0316, 0317). 2026-09-06.

decls.name: SigmaC
decls.why: The odd envelope at complex argument, `∫₋₁¹ x·P(x)·sinh(w x) dx`.

decls.name: Psi
decls.why: `Ψ(s) = ∫₋₁¹ x·P(x)·sin(s x) dx`, entry 302's transform of the envelope.

decls.name: G
decls.why: The tuned window: `(u/h)·P(u/h)·cos(γu)`, read on `[−h, h]`.

decls.name: ghat
decls.why: Its transform, `∫₋ₕʰ G(u)·e^{zu} du`.

decls.name: P_even
decls.why: The window `P` is even: `P (-x) = P x`.

decls.name: xP_odd
decls.why: The envelope `x·P x` is odd: its value at `-x` is the negative of its value at `x`.

decls.name: continuous_xP
decls.why: Helper: the envelope `x ↦ x·P x` is continuous.
decls.proves: Continuous fun x : ℝ => x * P x

decls.proves: Real.pi * δ ^ 2 * (Z.card : ℝ) ≤ 3 * (15 * Real.log T + 73) * ∫ u in (σ - δ)..(1 + δ), ∫ t in (1:ℝ)..T, ‖MollifiedMean.f X ((u : ℂ) + Complex.I * (t : ℂ))‖ ^ 2

header: ZeroSum — step 4: the dyadic zero-count arithmetic under hNT. The hNT leaf is IEANTN's `riemannZeta.Riemann_vonMangoldt_bound b₁ b₂ b₃` (Rosser Th. 19 shape; the literature instantiates (0.137, 0.443, 6.1)). O69 measured what it asserts: the angle count IS the logarithm curve, the fluctuation under 2 windings in 10⁵. This module proves the counting arithmetic that the explicit-formula assembly (step 5) consumes:

decls.name: log_two_pi_le
decls.why: `log(2π) ≤ 2`, i.e. `2π ≤ e²`. Carries the main-term constant.

decls.name: RvM_mono
decls.why: The RvM band is monotone in `T` on `[2, ∞)` for nonnegative `b₁, b₂`.
decls.proves: riemannZeta.RvM b₁ b₂ b₃ T ≤ riemannZeta.RvM b₁ b₂ b₃ T'

decls.name: abs_mainterm_le
decls.why: The main term is at most `(T/2π)(log T + 3) + 7/8` in absolute value: `|log(T/2π)| ≤ log T + log 2π ≤ log T + 2`.

decls.name: N_abs_le
decls.why: The T·log T majorant under hNT, explicit: `|N(T)| ≤ (T/2π)(log T + 3) + RvM(T) + 7/8`. This is the count shape the census needs — the unconditional route only gives `T^(3/2)`.
decls.proves: |riemannZeta.N T| ≤ T / (2 * Real.pi) * (Real.log T + 3) + riemannZeta.RvM b₁ b₂ b₃ T + 7 / 8

decls.name: sum_range_add_one
decls.why: Gauss sum over ℝ: `Σ_{j<n} (j+1) = n(n+1)/2`.

decls.name: sum_inv_pow_two_le
decls.why: Geometric tail: `Σ_{j<n} (2^j)⁻¹ ≤ 2`.

decls.name: dyadic_abs_N_sum_le
decls.why: The dyadic zero-count sum under hNT — the (log T)² arithmetic: `Σ_{j≤K} (2^j)⁻¹·|N(2^(j+1))| ≤ (log 2/2π)(K+1)(K+2) + 3(K+1)/π + 2(RvM(2^(K+1)) + 7/8)`. Leading constant `log 2/2π`: the classical `Σ 1/γ ~ (log T)²/4π` up to the dyadic overcount.
decls.proves: (∑ j ∈ range (K + 1), ((2 : ℝ) ^ j)⁻¹ * |riemannZeta.N ((2 : ℝ) ^ (j + 1))|) ≤ Real.log 2 / (2 * Real.pi) * (K + 1) * (K + 2) + 3 * (K + 1) / Real.pi + 2 * (riemannZeta.RvM b₁ b₂ b₃ ((2 : ℝ) ^ (K + 1)) + 7 / 8)

header: ZeroSummable — block C6b of `lean_stage3/design/carlson.md`. 2026-11-23. The zeros of ζ to the right of a line `Re s = σ > 1/2` have summable weights `m(ρ)/|ρ|`. A zero in the shell `2^j ≤ |Im ρ| < 2^(j+1)` has order at most `103·(j + 1)` (the local count of `Stage3.zeta_local_zero_count`, with conjugation for the lower half plane) and modulus at least `2^j`. `ZeroDensity.zero_density` at height `2^(j+1) + 2`, applied to the upper half and to the conjugates of the lower half, bounds the number of zeros in the shell…

decls.name: w
decls.why: The weight of a nontrivial zero: its order over its modulus.

decls.name: w_nonneg
decls.why: The weight `w ρ` of a nontrivial zero is nonnegative.

decls.name: mem_nt
decls.why: A nontrivial zero is a zero of ζ with real part strictly between zero and one.

decls.name: order_le_log_pos
decls.why: A nontrivial zero with real part above `1/2` and imaginary part at least two has order at most `15·log(Im ρ + 1) + 73`.

decls.name: order_le_log
decls.why: A nontrivial zero with real part above `1/2` and `|Im ρ| ≥ 2` has order at most `15·log(|Im ρ| + 1) + 73`.

decls.name: order_le_shell
decls.why: A nontrivial zero with real part above `1/2` in the shell `2^j ≤ |Im ρ| < 2^(j+1)`, `j ≥ 1`, has order at most `103·(j + 1)`.

decls.name: card_shell_le
decls.why: Given the zero-density bound at all heights from `T₀`, a finite set of nontrivial zeros with `Re ρ ≥ σ` in the shell `2^j ≤ |Im ρ| < 2^(j+1)`, `j ≥ 1`, `2^(j+1) + 2 ≥ T₀`, has at most `2·C·(2^(j+1) + 2)^θ` elements.
needs: hd : ∀ T : ℝ, T₀ ≤ T → ∀ Z : Finset ℂ, (∀ ρ ∈ Z, riemannZeta ρ = 0 ∧ σ ≤ ρ.re ∧ ρ.re < 1 ∧ 2 ≤ ρ.im ∧ ρ.im ≤ T - 2) → (Z.card : ℝ) ≤ C * T ^ θ

decls.name: shell_sum_le
decls.why: Under the same hypotheses, with `σ > 1/2`, the weights over a finite set of zeros in the shell `2^j ≤ |Im ρ| < 2^(j+1)` sum to at most `2·C·(2^(j+1) + 2)^θ·103·(j + 1)/2^j`.
needs: hd : ∀ T : ℝ, T₀ ≤ T → ∀ Z : Finset ℂ, (∀ ρ ∈ Z, riemannZeta ρ = 0 ∧ σ ≤ ρ.re ∧ ρ.re < 1 ∧ 2 ≤ ρ.im ∧ ρ.im ≤ T - 2) → (Z.card : ℝ) ≤ C * T ^ θ

decls.name: shell_bound_le
decls.why: For `C ≥ 0` the shell bound `2·C·(2^(j+1) + 2)^θ·103·(j + 1)/2^j` is at most `206·C·4^θ'·(j + 1)·(2^θ'/2)^j` with `θ' = max θ 0`.

decls.name: summable_shell
decls.why: For `0 ≤ r < 1` and any constant `K`, the series `Σ_j K·(j + 1)·r^j` converges.
decls.proves: Summable fun j : ℕ => K * (((j : ℝ) + 1) * r ^ j)

decls.name: dyadic_index
decls.why: For `x ≥ 1` the index `k = Nat.log 2 ⌊x⌋₊` satisfies `2^k ≤ x < 2^(k+1)`.

decls.name: sum_le_const
decls.why: For `1/2 < σ ≤ 1` there is one constant bounding the sum of the weights `m(ρ)/|ρ|` over every finite set of nontrivial zeros with `Re ρ ≥ σ`.
decls.proves: ∃ M : ℝ, ∀ v : Finset NontrivialZeros, (∀ ρ ∈ v, σ ≤ (ρ : ℂ).re) → ∑ ρ ∈ v, w ρ ≤ M

decls.name: summable_order_div
decls.why: The zeros right of a line have summable weights. For `σ > 1/2` the weights `m(ρ)/|ρ|` of the nontrivial zeros of ζ with `Re ρ ≥ σ` form a summable family.
decls.proves: Summable fun ρ : {ρ : Kadiri.NontrivialZeros // σ ≤ ((ρ : Kadiri.NontrivialZeros) : ℂ).re} => ((riemannZeta.order ((ρ : Kadiri.NontrivialZeros) : ℂ) : ℤ) : ℝ) / ‖((ρ : Kadiri.NontrivialZeros) : ℂ)‖

decls.name: norm_coef
decls.why: The norm of the cell coefficient `LadderMean.coef ρ` is the weight `m(ρ)/|ρ|`.

decls.name: summable_norm_coef
decls.why: For `σ > 1/2` and any set `S` of nontrivial zeros all with `Re ρ ≥ σ`, the norms of the cell coefficients `‖LadderMean.coef ρ‖` are summable over `S`.

header: ZetaEM — block C3 of `lean_stage3/design/carlson.md`. 2026-11-23. Euler–Maclaurin for the Riemann zeta function to any order `k ≥ 1` on `Re s > 0`, with the remainder bounded. The periodic Bernoulli function `P_k(x) = B_k({x})` has right derivative `k·P_{k-1}` everywhere and is continuous for `k ≠ 1`, so one integration by parts on `[a, b]` needs no splitting at the integers. Passing `b → ∞` gives the step `(k+1)·I_k = −B_{k+1}({a})·a^{−s−k} + (s+k)·I_{k+1}` for the tail integrals `I_k(a, s) = ∫_{x>a} P_k(x)·x^{−s−…

decls.name: emInt
decls.why: The order-`k` tail integral `∫_{x>N} B_k({x})·x^{−(s+k)}`.

decls.name: emCoef
decls.why: The coefficient `−s(s+1)⋯(s+k−1)/k!` of the order-`k` remainder.

decls.name: emTerm
decls.why: The boundary term `s(s+1)⋯(s+j−1)·B_{j+1}(0)/(j+1)!·N^{−(s+j)}`.

decls.name: emBoundary
decls.why: The boundary sum `Σ_{1 ≤ j < k} emTerm j N s`.

decls.name: emRem
decls.why: The order-`k` remainder `emCoef k s · emInt k N s`.

decls.name: bernBound
decls.why: The supremum of `|B_k|` on `[0, 1]`.

decls.name: hasDerivWithinAt_fract
decls.why: The fractional part has right derivative `1` at every real `x`.

decls.name: continuous_bernoulliFun_fract
decls.why: For `k ≠ 1` the periodic Bernoulli function `x ↦ B_k({x})` is continuous.
decls.proves: Continuous (fun x : ℝ ↦ bernoulliFun k (Int.fract x))

decls.name: abs_bernoulliFun_fract_le
decls.why: The periodic Bernoulli function is bounded in absolute value by `bernBound k`.

decls.name: bernBound_nonneg
decls.why: The bound `bernBound k` is nonnegative.

decls.name: measurable_bern
decls.why: The periodic Bernoulli function is measurable.
decls.proves: Measurable (fun x : ℝ ↦ bernoulliFun k (Int.fract x))

decls.name: integrableOn_bern_cpow
decls.why: For `Re w < −1` and `0 < a`, the function `B_k({x})·x^w` is integrable on `(a, ∞)`.
decls.proves: IntegrableOn (fun x : ℝ ↦ ((bernoulliFun k (Int.fract x) : ℝ) : ℂ) * (x:ℂ) ^ w) (Ioi a)

decls.name: norm_integral_bern_cpow_le
decls.why: For `Re w < −1` and `0 < a`, the integral of `B_k({x})·x^w` over `(a, ∞)` has norm at most `bernBound k · a^{Re w + 1}/(−(Re w + 1))`.
decls.proves: ‖∫ x in Ioi a, ((bernoulliFun k (Int.fract x) : ℝ) : ℂ) * (x:ℂ) ^ w‖ ≤ bernBound k * (-a ^ (w.re + 1) / (w.re + 1))

decls.name: interval_ibp
decls.why: One integration by parts on `[a, b]`: for `k ≥ 1`, `0 < a ≤ b` and `Re s + k > 1`, `(k+1)·∫_a^b P_k x^{−(s+k)}` is the boundary term of `P_{k+1} x^{−(s+k)}` plus `(s+k)·∫_a^b P_{k+1} x^{−(s+k+1)}`.
decls.proves: ((k:ℂ) + 1) * ∫ x in a..b, ((bernoulliFun k (Int.fract x) : ℝ) : ℂ) * (x:ℂ) ^ (-(s + k)) = ((bernoulliFun (k+1) (Int.fract b) : ℝ) : ℂ) * (b:ℂ) ^ (-(s + k)) - ((bernoulliFun (k+1) (Int.fract a) : ℝ) : ℂ) * (a:ℂ) ^ (-(s + k)) + (s + k) * ∫ x in a..b, ((bernoulliFun (k+1) (Int.fract x) : ℝ) : ℂ) * (x:ℂ) ^ (-(s + ((k+1 : ℕ) : ℂ)))

decls.name: tail_ibp
decls.why: The step on the tail: for `k ≥ 1`, `0 < a` and `Re s + k > 1`, `(k+1)·I_k(a) = −B_{k+1}({a})·a^{−(s+k)} + (s+k)·I_{k+1}(a)`.
decls.proves: ((k:ℂ) + 1) * ∫ x in Ioi a, ((bernoulliFun k (Int.fract x) : ℝ) : ℂ) * (x:ℂ) ^ (-(s + k)) = -(((bernoulliFun (k+1) (Int.fract a) : ℝ) : ℂ) * (a:ℂ) ^ (-(s + k))) + (s + k) * ∫ x in Ioi a, ((bernoulliFun (k+1) (Int.fract x) : ℝ) : ℂ) * (x:ℂ) ^ (-(s + ((k+1 : ℕ) : ℂ)))

decls.name: emInt_step
decls.why: The recursion for the tail integrals: for `k ≥ 1`, `0 < N` and `Re s + k > 1`, `(k+1)·I_k(N, s) = −B_{k+1}(0)·N^{−(s+k)} + (s+k)·I_{k+1}(N, s)`.
decls.proves: ((k:ℂ) + 1) * emInt k N s = -((bernoulliFun (k+1) 0 : ℂ) * (N:ℂ) ^ (-(s + k))) + (s + k) * emInt (k+1) N s

decls.name: emRem_step
decls.why: The remainder step: the order-`k` remainder is the `k`-th boundary term plus the order-`(k+1)` remainder, for `k ≥ 1`, `0 < N`, `Re s + k > 1`.
decls.proves: emRem k N s = emTerm k N s + emRem (k+1) N s

decls.name: sum_range_succ_eq_sum_Icc
decls.why: The sum `Σ_{n ≤ N} 1/n^s` equals `Σ_{n ∈ [1, N]} n^{−s}` for `s ≠ 0`.
decls.proves: ∑ n ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), 1 / (n : ℂ) ^ s = ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, (n : ℂ) ^ (-s)

decls.name: sum_range_eq_sum_Icc
decls.why: The shifted sum `Σ_{n < N} 1/(n+1)^s` equals `Σ_{n ∈ [1, N]} n^{−s}`.
decls.proves: ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, 1 / ((n:ℂ) + 1) ^ s = ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, (n : ℂ) ^ (-s)

decls.name: zeta_eq_em_one
decls.why: The order-one formula: for `0 < N`, `Re s > 0`, `s ≠ 1`, `ζ(s) = Σ_{n ∈ [1,N]} n^{−s} − N^{1−s}/(1−s) − N^{−s}/2 − s·I_1(N, s)`.
decls.proves: riemannZeta s = ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, (n : ℂ) ^ (-s) - (N:ℂ) ^ (1 - s) / (1 - s) - (N:ℂ) ^ (-s) / 2 - s * emInt 1 N s

decls.name: zeta_eq_em
decls.why: Euler–Maclaurin of order `k`: for every `k ≥ 1`, `0 < N`, `Re s > 0`, `s ≠ 1`, `ζ(s) = Σ_{n ∈ [1,N]} n^{−s} − N^{1−s}/(1−s) − N^{−s}/2 + emBoundary k N s + emRem k N s`.
decls.proves: riemannZeta s = ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, (n : ℂ) ^ (-s) - (N:ℂ) ^ (1 - s) / (1 - s) - (N:ℂ) ^ (-s) / 2 + emBoundary k N s + emRem k N s

decls.name: norm_emInt_le
decls.why: The order-`k` tail integral has norm at most `bernBound k · N^{1−σ−k}/(σ+k−1)` when `σ + k > 1`.
decls.proves: ‖emInt k N s‖ ≤ bernBound k * ((N:ℝ) ^ (1 - s.re - k) / (s.re + k - 1))

decls.name: norm_remainder_le
decls.why: The remainder bound: for `σ + k > 1` and `0 < N`, the order-`k` remainder has norm at most `(∏_{i<k}‖s+i‖/k!)·bernBound k·N^{1−σ−k}/(σ+k−1)`.
decls.proves: ‖emRem k N s‖ ≤ (∏ i ∈ Finset.range k, ‖s + i‖) / k.factorial * (bernBound k * ((N:ℝ) ^ (1 - s.re - k) / (s.re + k - 1)))

decls.name: norm_emTerm
decls.why: The `j`-th boundary term has norm `∏_{i<j}‖s+i‖·|B_{j+1}(0)|/(j+1)!·N^{−σ−j}`.
decls.proves: ‖emTerm j N s‖ = (∏ i ∈ Finset.range j, ‖s + i‖) * |bernoulliFun (j+1) 0| / (j+1).factorial * (N:ℝ) ^ (-s.re - j)

decls.name: prod_norm_le
decls.why: For `i < j ≤ k`, the product `∏_{i<j}‖s+i‖` is at most `(‖s‖+k)^j`.
decls.proves: ∏ i ∈ Finset.range j, ‖s + i‖ ≤ (‖s‖ + k) ^ j

decls.name: emConst
decls.why: The constant of the corollary: `1/2 + Σ_{1 ≤ j < k} |B_{j+1}(0)|/(j+1)! + bernBound k/k!`.

decls.name: norm_zeta_sub_partial_le
decls.proves: ‖riemannZeta s - ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, (n : ℂ) ^ (-s) + (N : ℂ) ^ (1 - s) / (1 - s)‖ ≤ emConst k * (N : ℝ) ^ (-s.re) * (1 + (‖s‖ + k) ^ k * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 - (k : ℝ)))

header: # Zeta growth on the strip `re > −1` (S3a — the load-bearing unknown of S3) Second-order Euler–Maclaurin: one integration by parts past PNT+'s `riemannZeta0`. The antiderivative `emA x = ({x} − {x}²)/2` of `⌊x⌋ + 1/2 − x` vanishes at every integer, so the per-interval boundary terms die and the new tail converges absolutely on `re s > −1`.

decls.name: emA
decls.why: The Euler–Maclaurin antiderivative: `({x} − {x}²)/2`.

decls.name: emA_nonneg
decls.why: The Euler–Maclaurin antiderivative `emA` is nonnegative at every real `x`.

decls.name: emA_le
decls.why: The Euler–Maclaurin antiderivative `emA` is at most `1/8` at every real `x`.

decls.name: emA_natCast
decls.why: The Euler–Maclaurin antiderivative `emA` vanishes at every natural number.

decls.name: emA_eq_poly
decls.why: On `[n, n+1]`, `emA` agrees with the polynomial `((x−n) − (x−n)²)/2` — including at the right endpoint, where both vanish.

decls.name: integrable_emA_tail
decls.why: The second-order tail integrand is integrable on `Ioi N` whenever `re s > −1`.
decls.proves: IntegrableOn (fun x : ℝ ↦ (emA x : ℂ) * (x : ℂ) ^ (-(s+2))) (Ioi (N:ℝ))

decls.name: interval_ibp
decls.why: The per-interval integration by parts. On `[n, n+1]` with `n ≥ 1`, the first-order tail integrand integrates to `(s+1)` times the second-order one — the boundary terms vanish at the integers.

decls.name: tail_ibp
decls.why: The tail identity on `Ioi N` for `re s > 0`: the per-interval IBP summed over adjacent intervals and passed to the limit.

decls.name: zeta1
decls.why: The continued Euler–Maclaurin form: every piece converges absolutely on `re s > −1`.

decls.name: zeta1_eq_zeta
decls.why: On `re s > 0` the continued form agrees with `ζ`.

decls.name: tail_differentiableAt
decls.why: The tail integral is differentiable in `s` on `re s > −1`: it is a Mellin transform of a bounded function vanishing near `0`.
decls.proves: DifferentiableAt ℂ (fun w : ℂ ↦ ∫ x in Ioi (N:ℝ), (emA x : ℂ) * (x:ℂ) ^ (-(w+2))) z

decls.name: stripRegion
decls.why: The strip on which the continued form lives.

decls.name: isOpen_stripRegion
decls.why: The strip region `{s | −1 < Re s ∧ s ≠ 1}` is open.

decls.name: preconnected_stripRegion
decls.why: The strip region `{s | −1 < Re s ∧ s ≠ 1}` is preconnected.

decls.name: zeta1_analyticOnNhd
decls.why: `zeta1` is analytic on the strip.

decls.name: zeta1_eq_zeta_strip
decls.why: The continuation: `zeta1 = ζ` on the whole strip.

decls.name: tail_norm_le
decls.why: Crude norm bound for the tail integral: `(1/4)·N^(−σ−1)`.

decls.name: sum_norm_le
decls.why: Crude bound for the shifted finite sum: `N·N^(1/2)`.

decls.name: zeta_growth_strip
decls.why: Polynomial growth of `ζ` on the strip — crude and explicit: `‖ζ(σ+it)‖ ≤ 15·t²` on `σ ∈ [−1/2, 4]`, `|t| ≥ 2`.

decls.name: sq_mul_zeta_analytic
decls.why: `(s−1)²·ζ` is analytic everywhere.
decls.proves: AnalyticAt ℂ (fun z : ℂ ↦ (z - 1)^2 * riemannZeta z) s

decls.name: sq_zeta_band_bound
decls.why: The Landau-ball input: `(s−1)²·ζ` bounded on the band `re ∈ [−1/2, 4]` by a power of the height — explicit for `|im| ≥ 2`, an existential constant absorbing the compact patch below.
decls.proves: ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ s : ℂ, -1/2 ≤ s.re → s.re ≤ 4 → ‖(s - 1)^2 * riemannZeta s‖ ≤ C * (2 + |s.im|) ^ 4

decls.name: hasCompactSupport_kOf
decls.why: If `G` has compact support, then the Weil test function `kOf G` has compact support.

decls.name: paperFT_kOf
decls.why: The term at a zero, in both languages.
decls.proves: paperFT (kOf G) (gammaOf ρ) = laplace G (-ρ) * laplace G (-(1 - ρ))

decls.name: weil_bridge
decls.why: The bridge. For a test function of Stage 3's class, the zero side of Weil's form, over the nontrivial zeros of `riemannZeta` with multiplicity, is summable and equals the prime side at `k = F ⋆ F̃`.
decls.proves: Summable (fun ρ : {ρ : ℂ | riemannZeta ρ = 0 ∧ 0 < ρ.re ∧ ρ.re < 1} => (((analyticOrderAt riemannZeta (ρ : ℂ)).toNat : ℕ) : ℂ) * (laplace G (-(ρ : ℂ)) * laplace G (-(1 - (ρ : ℂ))))) ∧ ∑' ρ : {ρ : ℂ | riemannZeta ρ = 0 ∧ 0 < ρ.re ∧ ρ.re < 1}, (((analyticOrderAt riemannZeta (ρ : ℂ)).toNat : ℕ) : ℂ) * (laplace G (-(ρ : ℂ)) * laplace G (-(1 - (ρ : ℂ)))) = primeSide (kOf G)

decls.name: ft
decls.why: The transform `∫ k(u) e^{izu} du`; zeta23's `paperFT`.

decls.name: kOfM
decls.why: `k = F ⋆ F̃` in Mathlib's convolution; zeta23's `weilTest` at `F = tiltF G`.

decls.name: primeSideM
decls.why: The prime side: the pole terms, minus the prime sum, plus the archimedean integral.

decls.name: StmtWeilBridge
decls.why: The bridge, as a statement.

decls.name: kOfM_eq
decls.why: The Weil test function in Mathlib's convolution, `kOfM G`, equals `kOf G`.

decls.name: primeSideM_eq
decls.why: The prime side written against Mathlib alone, `primeSideM k`, equals `primeSide k`.

decls.name: stmtWeilBridge_holds
decls.why: The bridge holds.
